title: Fidelity Strategist Stays Bullish as Bitcoin Dips Below $58K — Here’s Why
summary: Bitcoin’s sell-off took it below the support level on a Fidelity strategist’s weekly chart. He remains bullish but warned that a fall well below the rising line would call his long-term outlook into question. How Far Below Support Would Bitcoin Have to Fall? Jurrien Timmer, Fidelity Investments’ dir...
content:
Bitcoin’s sell-off took it below the support level on a Fidelity strategist’s weekly chart. He remains bullish but warned that a fall well below the rising line would call his long-term outlook into question.

Key Takeaways

  • Timmer cited bitcoin’s four-year cycle and his power law model as reasons to stay bullish.
  • He found bitcoin’s return to the model’s support line discouraging.
  • He warned that a fall well below support would call his entire framework into question.

How Far Below Support Would Bitcoin Have to Fall?

Jurrien Timmer, Fidelity Investments’ director of global macro, reaffirmed his bullish outlook for bitcoin after the Nov. 20 drop below $58,000. The strategist wrote on X:

“I remain bullish on bitcoin based on its four-year cycle and Power Law math, but it’s a bit disheartening that we are back again sitting on that power law support curve.”

A power law describes a relationship in which doubling one quantity multiplies another by a fixed factor. Timmer applies that relationship to bitcoin’s age and price. The lower curve on his chart estimates where the price may find support as the network ages.

The weekly chart put bitcoin at $64,679 on Nov. 15, above the model’s $62,617 support line. Five days later, the strategist placed support near $62,000 and described it as rising. He gave no specific price or percentage decline that would change his view.

Timmer added: “If bitcoin’s price were to ever fall well below this support line (currently at $62k and rising), it would put my entire framework in doubt. Never a dull moment!”

Bitcoin Dipped Below $58,000 on Nov. 20

Bitcoin had traded above $61,000 earlier on Nov. 20 before losing nearly $3,000 between 11 a.m. and noon Eastern. The slide later reached about $57,960, roughly 7.4% below the support level on Timmer’s Nov. 15 chart. As of 8:46 p.m. Eastern, bitcoin was down about 5% over 24 hours and more than 13% over seven days.

In February, the strategist identified an attractive entry point near $65,000. Bitcoin subsequently touched about $57,800 in late June before recovering over the summer.

By September, bitcoin was back near $80,000. The strategist saw a possible path to $100,000 after bitcoin formed two lows. The $100,000 projection depended on a breakout above $80,000.

Does Bitcoin Still Follow a Four-Year Cycle?

The strategist also drew on the historical pattern of bitcoin’s market peaks and downturns. Under the bitcoin halving schedule, the network cuts the amount of new bitcoin miners receive per block in half every 210,000 blocks.

Fidelity Digital Assets analyst Zack Wainwright examined the four-year market cycle in February and found that bitcoin’s volatility had declined even as its price climbed above $126,000 in October 2025. Earlier peaks typically coincided with widening price swings.

In January 2026, just months after the record, Wainwright counted 17 occasions when bitcoin’s volatility over the preceding year reached a new low. Wainwright concluded that the familiar four-year pattern may no longer apply.

title: Peter Schiff Warns of Weekend Crypto Crash Sending ETH to $1K
summary: Ether briefly fell below the support level Peter Schiff identified six days earlier before trading back above it by Friday evening. He warned that a broader crypto selloff over the weekend could push it back toward its 2022 low by Monday. Schiff Warns Ether Could Hit $1,000 by Monday Economist and g...
content:
Ether briefly fell below the support level Peter Schiff identified six days earlier before trading back above it by Friday evening. He warned that a broader crypto selloff over the weekend could push it back toward its 2022 low by Monday.

Key Takeaways

  • Ether traded at $1,618.84 Friday evening, down 8.11% in 24 hours.
  • Peter Schiff’s $1,000 forecast implied a further drop of about 38.2%.
  • Bets on higher ether prices accounted for 87.73% of $427.51 million in liquidations.

Schiff Warns Ether Could Hit $1,000 by Monday

Economist and gold advocate Peter Schiff warned on Nov. 20 that a weekend crypto crash could send ether to $1,000 by Monday, Nov. 23, after it broke below $1,600.

“Ethereum broke below key support at $1,600. It just traded below $1,580, down 16.5% in the six days since I issued this warning,” he wrote, adding:

“There is a real risk of a crypto crash over the weekend that sends ether to $1,000 by Monday.”

At 8:33 p.m. EST on Nov. 20, ether traded at $1,618.84, down $142.92, or 8.11%, over 24 hours. The ETH price chart showed a 16.13% decline over the past week, a 34.46% loss over the past month, and a 42.78% drop over the past year. From the evening price, a decline to Schiff’s $1,000 level would amount to another $618.84 per ether, or about 38.2%.

Why Schiff Singled Out $1,600

Schiff compared bitcoin with Ethereum’s native asset, ether, in his Nov. 14 warning. The gold advocate wrote:

“It’s not just bitcoin that’s about to crash. Check out Ethereum. That chart looks even more ominous.”

The monthly Bitstamp chart he shared showed an upward-sloping line extending from ether’s June 2022 low. Schiff placed that trend line near $1,600 in November and identified the 2022 low, just below $1,000, as the next level where buyers might step in. If that low gave way, he saw no further support until a lower line on the chart.

At the time, Schiff’s argument centered on what might happen if ETH crossed $1,600. His Friday update said that threshold had been breached and added a time frame to his forecast. He now saw a risk that ETH could reach $1,000 within three days.

ETH Liquidations Reach $427.51 Million in 24 Hours

When Schiff issued his first warning, a broader weekend crypto selloff was already underway. The market lost more than $130 billion in value from Nov. 13 to Nov. 15. By that Sunday, ether was down 19% over seven days, compared with a 14.5% decline for bitcoin.

Selling intensified again on Nov. 20, when bitcoin fell to $58,701 on Bitstamp. An earlier report put liquidations across crypto markets at $1.53 billion over 24 hours. More than $1.38 billion came from leveraged bets that prices would rise, including more than $494 million in bitcoin positions.

By Friday evening, Coinglass had recorded $427.51 million in ETH liquidations over 24 hours, or 2.27 times the seven-day average. Long positions, or bets on higher prices, accounted for $375.07 million, or 87.73% of the total. Short positions accounted for $52.45 million. Binance accounted for $202.94 million, or 47.47% of the 24-hour total, followed by Hyperliquid at $61.90 million and Gate at $44.95 million. Coinglass reported that 25,371 traders worldwide had positions liquidated. The largest single ETH liquidation was $11.98 million.

title: Binance Hackers Move $860 Million in Ether as Bitcoin Laundering Surges
summary: Hackers linked to North Korea have moved approximately $860 million in ether stolen from Binance over the past four days, while dramatically accelerating efforts to obscure the origins of bitcoin obtained through cryptocurrency swaps, according to new findings from blockchain analytics firm Elliptic...
content:
Hackers linked to North Korea have moved approximately $860 million in ether stolen from Binance over the past four days, while dramatically accelerating efforts to obscure the origins of bitcoin obtained through cryptocurrency swaps, according to new findings from blockchain analytics firm Elliptic.

Key Takeaways

  • Binance hackers moved approximately $860 million in stolen ether between Nov. 17–20, redistributing 488,000 ETH across smaller wallets and converting roughly $70 million into bitcoin.
  • Bitcoin laundering activity surged dramatically, with approximately 2,080 BTC entering coinjoin transactions over four days. Elliptic has traced the broader operation across more than 27,000 wallets and 16 blockchains.
  • Billions in stolen funds remain dormant or frozen, including $2.35 billion still held in hacker-linked wallets and $2.85 billion frozen or seized.

In a report updated Friday, Nov. 20, Elliptic revealed that five of the nine largest ether wallets associated with October’s record $6.3 billion theft have been emptied since Tuesday. The transfers involved approximately 488,000 ETH—valued near $860 million at the time of the update—marking the first significant movement from those addresses since Oct. 30.

The hackers transferred 74,880 ETH on Nov. 17, followed by 78,415 ETH on Nov. 18, 137,602 ETH on Nov. 19, and another 197,460 ETH on Friday. The funds were redistributed into smaller holdings of approximately 12,000 ETH each, apparently preparing them for further laundering.

Most of the relocated ether remains untouched, although approximately 39,000 ETH, has already been exchanged for about 1,100 BTC since Tuesday. Elliptic said the perpetrators are routing the transactions through THORChain, breaking the funds into smaller transfers before converting them into bitcoin.

The activity resembles tactics employed following North Korea’s $1.5 billion Bybit hack in February 2025, when stolen ether was similarly converted into bitcoin before being moved through additional laundering channels.

Bitcoin Mixing Accelerates Dramatically

The latest developments also reveal a surge in bitcoin mixing, a technique intended to make cryptocurrency transactions more difficult to trace.

According to Elliptic, approximately 480 BTC entered coinjoin transactions on Nov. 17, exceeding the amount processed during the preceding two weeks combined. That figure increased to 590 BTC on Nov. 18, followed by 520 BTC on Thursday and another 490 BTC by late Friday morning.

Altogether, at least 2,310 BTC, valued at approximately $149 million as of the update, has entered coinjoins since the beginning of November, with roughly 90% of that activity occurring during the past four days.

Elliptic identified Kruw, a coordinator commonly used by Wasabi Wallet users, as facilitating nearly all those coinjoin transactions. The coordinator organizes transactions involving multiple participants without taking custody of their bitcoin, making it harder for investigators to establish connections between sending and receiving addresses.

Notably, the original 18,270 BTC stolen directly from Binance has remained stationary since the attack. The bitcoin currently undergoing laundering was instead obtained through conversions of other stolen assets, including ether, XRP and solana.

Billions Remain Unspent as Binance Recovers

The latest findings mark another escalation in a sprawling operation that Elliptic has now traced through more than 27,000 wallets, at least 16 blockchains, approximately 55 cryptocurrency services, and 90,000 transactions.

Despite those movements, roughly $2.35 billion remains in wallets associated with the theft, while another $2.85 billion has been frozen or seized. Elliptic believes only a negligible amount of the stolen cryptocurrency has actually been converted into spendable funds.

The company suggested that North Korean operatives likely retain control of the dormant holdings, although some actively laundered funds could have been transferred to Chinese money laundering networks.

As previously reported by Bitcoin.com News, the laundering operation initially involved approximately 12,000 wallets within four days of the Oct. 29 breach. Subsequent investigations uncovered increasingly elaborate techniques, including the creation of virtually worthless meme coins to complicate blockchain tracing.

Investigators including the FBI have attributed the attack to North Korea’s state-sponsored TraderTraitor hacking group, part of the broader Lazarus cybercrime ecosystem. Meanwhile, Binance has compensated users for the losses. Co-CEO Richard Teng previously said the company had committed more than $6.34 billion in corporate resources to cover the stolen assets, while acknowledging that attackers had bypassed normal wallet approval controls.

Bitcoin.com News reported on Nov. 14 that Binance had restored withdrawals across 87 blockchain networks, with plans to reopen remaining services.

Elliptic expects the hackers to continue exchanging ether for bitcoin and eventually attempt to cash out through crypto exchanges and over-the-counter brokers. However, the firm’s analysis suggests that converting the enormous holdings into usable funds could take months, leaving investigators additional opportunities to intercept the proceeds.

title: Strategy, Coinbase Shares Battered as Bitcoin Price Hits 2-Year Low and AI Stocks Bleed
summary: Crypto-related equities suffered punishing weekly losses as bitcoin plunged below $58,000 and a widespread technology sell-off pushed major Wall Street indexes into correction territory.   Shares of cryptocurrency companies plunged during a tumultuous week on Wall Street, with Strategy, Coinbase, an...
content:
Crypto-related equities suffered punishing weekly losses as bitcoin plunged below $58,000 and a widespread technology sell-off pushed major Wall Street indexes into correction territory.

Key Takeaways

  • Crypto stocks plunged this week, with Strategy falling approximately 30%, Coinbase and Robinhood both sliding 20%, and Bitmine losing 26% amid a broader market selloff.
  • Bitcoin sank to $57,799.29 on Friday, hitting its lowest price in more than two years after losing roughly 15% over the past week.
  • Wall Street’s AI-driven selloff intensified, with the Nasdaq tumbling roughly 10% for the week, Nvidia plunging nearly 14% on Friday, and newly public Anthropic falling following its big IPO.

Shares of cryptocurrency companies plunged during a tumultuous week on Wall Street, with Strategy, Coinbase, and other prominent industry stocks posting double-digit declines as bitcoin hit its lowest price since September 2024 and investors fled artificial intelligence investments.

Strategy (MSTR), the world’s largest corporate bitcoin holder, finished Friday at $77.80 per share, down approximately 30% from the previous week’s closing price of $111.62. The company has been particularly vulnerable to bitcoin’s slide, with the cryptocurrency now trading well below Strategy’s average acquisition cost of approximately $75,446 per coin. Friday’s closing price was the lowest since February 2024.

Coinbase (COIN) shares closed Friday at $101.97, down roughly 20% for the week and marking a roughly three-year low for the exchange’s shares. Robinhood (HOOD), which has substantial exposure to cryptocurrency trading, shed about 20% in the last week to finish at $62.17, while ether treasury company Bitmine Immersion Technologies (BMNR) dropped approximately 26% to $12.98.

Stablecoin issuer Circle (CRCL) and Galaxy Digital (GLXY) also suffered significant weekly declines, highlighting the breadth of selling across companies involved in cryptocurrency trading, investing, and digital asset treasuries.

Bitcoin Plunges Below $58,000 as November Rout Deepens

The equity losses accompanied another brutal week for bitcoin, which plunged to $57,799.29 on Friday, setting not only a 2026 low but also the lowest price registered since September 2024.

At a recent price near $59,000, bitcoin has lost approximately 15% over the past week and 31% over the last month, erasing its late-summer recovery and deepening a sell-off that has wiped out more than half its value since the cryptocurrency reached a record $126,080 in October 2025.

The decline puts bitcoin on course for its seventh consecutive losing week, potentially its longest weekly losing streak since 2022. November is also shaping up as one of the cryptocurrency’s worst months since the 2022 crypto market collapse, with the latest losses bringing bitcoin back to levels that previously attracted buyers during the summer.

Institutional demand has weakened considerably. U.S. spot bitcoin exchange-traded funds recorded approximately $582 million in net outflows Thursday, including $541 million withdrawn from BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust. Meanwhile, Friday’s cryptocurrency rout triggered $1.9 billion in leveraged position liquidations over the last 24 hours as of this writing, per data from Coinglass, predominantly affecting traders betting on rising prices.

Prominent altcoins have seen similar price declines as bitcoin over the last week, with some taking even harder hits: Ether (ETH) is down 18% over the same span, with zcash (ZEC) falling nearly 24%.

AI Stocks Lead Wall Street’s Collapse

Cryptocurrency companies were hardly alone in suffering substantial losses. The broader U.S. stock market experienced its worst week in approximately 19 months as investors reassessed lofty artificial intelligence valuations, enormous data-center expenditures, and the prospect of additional Federal Reserve interest-rate increases.

The technology-heavy Nasdaq Composite plunged 5.3% Friday, finishing at 22,617.73 and bringing its weekly decline to approximately 10%. The S&P 500 shed 3.7% to close at 6,910.39, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 1.9% to 48,147.33. All three benchmarks ended the week more than 10% below their respective record highs, meeting the conventional definition of a market correction.

AI chipmaking giant Nvidia (NVDA) was among the hardest-hit major companies, plunging nearly 14% Friday and extending a decline that has wiped out substantial shareholder value in recent weeks. Over the last month, shares have fallen 42% amid a corporate crisis that saw founder and CEO Jensen Huang depart over reported extramarital affairs with employees and a suspected Chinese spy.

Rival chipmakers AMD, Broadcom, and Micron also suffered steep losses as investors questioned whether the industry’s massive spending on artificial intelligence infrastructure could continue producing sufficient returns.

Even Anthropic’s historic initial public offering failed to restore confidence. The maker of the Claude chatbot completed the largest IPO on record Thursday, raising approximately $81 billion. Its shares initially surged above $111 before closing their debut session at $97.17, approximately 17% above the $83 offering price.

Anthropic stock subsequently fell more than 8% Friday, demonstrating how quickly investor enthusiasm has deteriorated despite continued demand for artificial intelligence services.

The market decline has been exacerbated by uncertainty surrounding AI-related capital expenditures, tighter financing conditions, and Nvidia’s leadership transition following Huang’s resignation earlier this month.

For cryptocurrency investors, the simultaneous weakness in bitcoin and technology equities underscores the difficulty of escaping a broader retreat from speculative investments. With both sectors facing substantial selling pressure, the next major test will be whether bitcoin can defend its summer lows while Wall Street attempts to stabilize following one of its most punishing weeks in recent years.

title: Bitcoin Price Slips to Lows Not Seen Since 2024, Nasdaq Plunges 5%
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bitcoin Price Slips to Lows Not Seen Since 2024, Nasdaq Plunges 5%
The bitcoin price slipped to near $58,300 on Friday afternoon, briefly dipping under its summer low, as a chip-led selloff sent the Nasdaq down about 5% and dragged crypto stocks and miners sharply lower.
This post ...
content:
The bitcoin price slid to near $58,300 on Friday afternoon, down about 6.2% over the past 24 hours, according to Look Into Bitcoin data, as a deepening selloff in chip and artificial intelligence stocks sent the Nasdaq down about 5% and pushed bitcoin just under its summer low.

Bitcoin broke below $60,000 late Friday morning, a few hours after this morning’s report had it near $61,500. Over the past 24 hours, the bitcoin price has traded between $57,655 and $62,562, a drop of about $3,880. Bitcoin is down about 25% in November, on pace for its worst month since June 2022.

Chip stocks drag Wall Street lower

Selling on Wall Street sped up through the afternoon. The Nasdaq Composite fell about 5% in late trading and the S&P 500 dropped about 3.5%. Yahoo Finance said the Nasdaq was on pace to close negative for the year, while the S&P 500 was poised to close in correction territory.

Chipmakers led the drop. Nvidia (NVDA) fell about 12.5% to near $128, and AMD, Broadcom and Micron also posted double-digit losses. Gold futures dropped nearly 5%. Treasury yields fell as traders rotated into bonds and defensive sectors such as consumer staples and healthcare, Reuters reported.

Anthropic (ANT) fell nearly 12% to around $86 on its first full day of trading, leaving it just above its $83 IPO price. The stock had closed its Thursday debut at $97.17 after raising $81.3 billion in the largest IPO of all time, CNBC reported.

Liquidations and outflows weigh on the bitcoin price

Leveraged traders were forced out as the bitcoin price broke support. About $1.53 billion in crypto bets were wiped out over 24 hours, with long positions making up $1.4 billion of that total. Bitcoin alone accounted for around $540 million, while ether fell more than 8% to around $1,600.

Bitcoin funds have been sellers, too. Investors have pulled roughly $3.5 billion from U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs so far this month, including $582 million on Thursday. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) accounted for $541.1 million of Thursday’s withdrawals, its largest one-day outflow on record.

Rate worries are adding pressure. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent pushed back Friday on calls for a half-point Federal Reserve hike in December. Traders still saw a more than 98% chance of a quarter-point increase, and some strategists warned that further hikes could deepen the selloff.

CoinShares head of research James Butterfill said the drop looks driven more by the AI stock selloff than by problems inside crypto. Bitcoin has increasingly traded alongside other growth assets that depend on easy money, he said.

The dip to $57,655 briefly took bitcoin just under its summer low near $57,700. It is also on track for a seventh straight weekly loss, its longest losing streak since 2022.

Crypto stocks extend losses

Strategy (MSTR) fell about 8.4% to near $78.90, adding to the losses after the stock fell for a sixth straight day on Thursday. Coinbase (COIN) dropped about 5.5% to near $103. Robinhood (HOOD) lost about 9.6% and Circle (CRCL) fell about 7.9%.

Bitcoin miners fared worst. MARA Holdings (MARA) sank about 17% to near $5.17, IREN (IREN) fell about 17% and CleanSpark (CLSK) dropped about 16%. Riot Platforms (RIOT) lost about 8.4%, and Galaxy Digital (GLXY) fell about 9.4%. Many miners have expanded into AI data centers, tying their shares to the chip selloff.

The bitcoin price is now down more than 50% from its record above $126,000, set in October 2025.

At the time of writing, the bitcoin price is near $58,300.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Wrapped Monero Token XMR1 Crashes After $13M Exploit, Founder Vows Repayment
summary: A security breach involving an Icelandic web hosting company has been linked to a multimillion-dollar exploit of XMR1, a tokenized version of Monero, leaving investors facing steep losses and raising questions about the security of wrapped cryptocurrencies. Wrapped Monero Crashes Near Zero XMR1, iss...
content:
A security breach involving an Icelandic web hosting company has been linked to a multimillion-dollar exploit of XMR1, a tokenized version of Monero, leaving investors facing steep losses and raising questions about the security of wrapped cryptocurrencies.

Key Takeaways

  • Wrapped Monero token XMR1 plunged more than 99% after hackers allegedly compromised a deployment key and extracted approximately $13.5 million through token sales on Hyperliquid.
  • Wagyu’s founder blamed the exploit on a cyberattack against Icelandic hosting provider 1984.hosting, which separately confirmed a major security breach. The founder pledged to reimburse affected users.
  • The underlying Monero blockchain was unaffected, but the incident highlights vulnerabilities in wrapped cryptocurrencies.

Wrapped Monero Crashes Near Zero

XMR1, issued by cross-chain trading project Wagyu, lost more than 99% of its value Friday, Nov. 20, after an attacker allegedly gained control of sensitive credentials used in the token’s deployment. The sell-off pushed XMR1 from nearly $500 to less than $1 within approximately half an hour.

Blockchain analytics firm Bitquery estimated that the attacker extracted roughly $13.5 million through a series of transactions involving Hyperliquid, the decentralized derivatives and trading platform.

Onchain records indicated that approximately 5.2 million XMR1 tokens were moved from a deployment wallet to an unfamiliar address before the attacker began unloading the assets. Roughly 364,000 tokens were subsequently sold through transactions involving 388 buyers, according to Bitquery.

The proceeds were initially converted into USDC before being exchanged for ether. Investigators subsequently identified approximately 7,350 ETH spread across three wallets. The sudden influx of tokens overwhelmed market demand, effectively destroying XMR1’s trading value.

Wagyu’s pseudonymous founder, PerpetualCow, pointed to a separate cybersecurity incident involving Iceland-based hosting provider 1984.hosting as the likely source of the compromise.

The founder claimed that a deployment key previously stored on a server had remained accessible through the hosting company’s infrastructure despite the server having been deleted. That allegedly allowed the attacker to obtain credentials capable of compromising XMR1.

The explanation has not been independently verified, although the hosting provider acknowledged suffering a serious cyberattack.

In a statement reported by Icelandic news outlet DV, 1984.hosting and the country’s cybersecurity response team, CERT-IS, disclosed that the provider had temporarily suspended its services following an intrusion affecting its systems.

The company characterized the attack as sophisticated and potentially widespread, with investigations underway to determine the full extent of the damage. It said operations would resume gradually after security assessments were completed.

PerpetualCow subsequently promised to cover customer losses using personal funds and indicated that Wagyu intends to restart its platform. Details about the compensation process and the timing of any potential recovery remain unclear.

“Everyone who lost money due to this will be refunded by me personally and Wagyu will re-launch at a later stage,” they wrote on X. “Give me some time please.”

XMR1 was developed to make Monero, a cryptocurrency known for its transaction privacy features, accessible through Hyperliquid’s trading ecosystem. Wrapped assets such as XMR1 seek to represent cryptocurrencies on networks where their native tokens cannot otherwise operate directly.

Importantly, the incident did not involve a breach of Monero itself. However, the cryptocurrency’s privacy protections complicate efforts to independently determine whether sufficient native XMR remains available to support outstanding wrapped tokens.

XMR was recently down about 9% on the day at a price near $451, amid a broader market plunge that brought bitcoin down to its lowest price since September 2024. Monero is down more than 25% over the last month.

The exploit adds to a growing list of security failures involving tokenized representations of established cryptocurrencies.

Bitcoin.com News previously reported that attackers exploited the Symbiosis bitcoin bridge in September, generating billions of unauthorized syBTC tokens while reportedly capturing approximately $336,000 in proceeds. Other incidents have exposed vulnerabilities affecting wrapped assets associated with the Liquid Network and Nomic.

Separately, a March exploit targeting Resolv Labs generated approximately $23 million in losses and destabilized its USR stablecoin, illustrating how weaknesses in privileged access and token issuance mechanisms can trigger substantial market disruptions.

The XMR1 episode highlights a fundamental distinction between holding cryptocurrencies directly and trading wrapped versions: even when the underlying blockchain remains secure, the systems responsible for issuing and managing tokenized representations can introduce additional points of failure.

title: Anthropic’s Two-Tier Debut: Who Got $83 Shares and Who Financed the $111.50 Open
summary:
Anthropic invited retail investors to participate in its historic IPO, but most retail traders faced the brick wall of geo and eligibility restrictions, becoming the exit liquidity for the opening pop. 
Anthropic sold 980 million Class A shares at $83 each before trading began under the ANT ticker o...
content:
2026-11-20T21:50:25.673+02:00

Friday, 20/11/2026 | 19:50 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • Broker eligibility rules and geographic exclusions split retail investors during Anthropic’s debut.
  • Vanda Research tracked a record $700M–$800M in debut-day retail volume against just $60M in net buying.

Anthropic invited retail investors to participate in its historic IPO, but most retail traders faced the brick wall of geo and eligibility restrictions, becoming the exit liquidity for the opening pop.

Anthropic sold 980 million Class A shares at $83 each before trading began under the ANT ticker on 19 November.

The company allocated 15% of the offering to retail accounts, but eventually millions of self-directed traders across excluded jurisdictions and brokerages were forced to wait for Nasdaq’s opening bell.

Those secondary-market buyers entered as the stock opened 34% higher at $111.50, only to absorb an immediate 13% intraday drawdown as shares faded to close at $97.17.

Retail Investors Were Geo-fenced and Condition-Fenced

Several brokers, including Charles Schwab, Fidelity, Robinhood, Trade-PMR, SoFi and Morgan Stanley’s E*TRADE allowed retail clients to participate in Anthropic's initial offering.

However, having an account with a participating broker was not enough to qualify as an IPO investor, as many set blocking conditions.

Thus, at Fidelity, eligible traders should have at least $25,000 in certain assets and subscribe for a minimum of 25 shares - $2,075 at $83 a share.

@Maximo8136151 That's correct. Brokerage clients with at least $25,000 in eligible assets can participate in this initial public offering (IPO). If you have any other questions, don't hesitate to let us know!

— Fidelity Investments (@Fidelity) November 10, 2026

Hargreaves Lansdown took applications from eligible UK clients from day one, with a minimum of £250. 45,811 applications were received with an average application of £6,661. Demand was so strong that clients ended up with 33.6% of the shares they requested.

Geo restrictions also applied: the prospectus covered retail investors from the UK, Switzerland, Australia, Canada, Japan and selected EU countries.

Secondary Buyers Absorbed the Post-Open Slide

Activity in the Czech Republic shows how retail investors have reacted in a market excluded from Anthropic's core offering. It also illustrates the prices and risks they faced in getting in after exchange trading began.

Clients of Patria, Fio and XTB entered after Nasdaq trading opened, immediately facing a price 34% above the IPO allocation.

title: Wrapped Monero token crashes 99.8% amid suspected $13.5M exploit
summary: Bitquery traced $13.5 million in suspicious sales of the wrapped Monero token, as its operator blamed a security breach and promised to reimburse affected traders.
content:
A wrapped version of Monero (XMR) plunged more than 99% on Hyperliquid on Friday after a wallet that received tokens from the deployer account sold approximately $13.5 million worth of the asset, according to blockchain analytics firm Bitquery.

The token, known as XMR1, fell from around $500 to $1 in roughly 30 minutes, a 99.8% decline, according to Bitquery. Wrapped tokens are designed to represent other cryptocurrencies on different blockchains, allowing them to be traded outside their native networks. The collapse affected XMR1 rather than Monero’s native cryptocurrency.

According to Bitquery’s onchain analysis, the wallet received 5.2 million XMR1 tokens from the deployer account before selling approximately $13.5 million worth of the asset on Friday.

The firm traced $13.28 million in USDC transferred to Arbitrum, where $13.22 million was exchanged for 7,467 Ether (ETH) through CoW Protocol. Most of the ETH was subsequently bridged to Ethereum.

Bitquery also found that proceeds from four hacks earlier in November, involving Across Protocol, Kava, Lighter and Safe, had been used to purchase approximately $6.6 million worth of XMR1, apparently as a route to native Monero. The firm said it found no onchain evidence linking those incidents to Friday’s suspected exploit.

Value of XMR1 purchases linked to funds from four November hacks. Source: Bitquery

Bitquery said its onchain investigation could not establish how the deployer account’s private key was obtained or who controlled it during the transfers, leaving the circumstances of the suspected compromise unconfirmed.

Related: Binance hacker moves nearly $600M in ETH, routes funds through THORChain, Chainflip

Wagyu operator blames suspected infrastructure breach

PerpetualCow, the pseudonymous operator of Wagyu, the service behind XMR1, attributed the collapse to an alleged breach of hosting provider 1984, claiming that customer data and internal server files had been exposed.

According to PerpetualCow, the XMR1 deployer key had been stored on a server that was subsequently deleted, but the hosting provider allegedly retained logs and files associated with it.

Source: Perpetual Cow

PerpetualCow also pledged to personally reimburse affected traders and said Wagyu would relaunch at a later date, although no timeline was provided.

Cointelegraph contacted the operator for additional details about the suspected breach and reimbursement plans but had not received a response by publication.

title: Bitcoin Hits Lowest Price Since 2024 After Peter Brandt Warns of Deflation
summary: Bitcoin plunged below $58,000 to hit its lowest price in over two years Friday as Peter Brandt warned that a sell-off across financial and raw material markets would likely lead to deflation. His forecast concerned the broader market, while the latest U.S. consumer-price data still showed inflation....
content:
Bitcoin plunged below $58,000 to hit its lowest price in over two years Friday as Peter Brandt warned that a sell-off across financial and raw material markets would likely lead to deflation. His forecast concerned the broader market, while the latest U.S. consumer-price data still showed inflation.

Key Takeaways

  • Bitcoin traded below $58,000 on Friday, marking its lowest price since September 2024.
  • The price fell more than 15% over a week and nearly 54% from its record.
  • Brandt predicted deflation as financial assets and commodities slid.

Bitcoin Breaks Below $58,000

Veteran trader Peter Brandt warned on Nov. 20 that financial-market and commodity declines would most likely lead to deflation, hours before bitcoin plunged below $58,000. His forecast concerned a potential drop in consumer prices across the economy rather than a specific bitcoin price target.

Financial markets trade assets such as stocks, bonds, and bitcoin. Raw material markets include metals, energy, and agricultural products. Brandt linked the sell-off across those markets to his forecast of positive returns on interest-bearing assets after accounting for deflation. He wrote:

“Not sure many are so aware, but we are witnessing in the financial and raw material markets a melt-down that most likely will lead to deflation, meaning positive interest rate return.”

At 2:20 p.m. EST on Nov. 20, the bitcoin price at $57,961 was down 7.6% over 24 hours, 15% over a week and 30.9% over a month. It was nearly 54% below its record of $126,080, set Oct. 6, 2025, falling to its lowest price seen since September 2024.

Metals Slump Alongside Financial Assets

At 2:05 p.m. EST on Nov. 20, indicative December metals prices put gold futures at $3,521 an ounce, silver futures at $41.27 an ounce and copper futures at $5.49 a pound. The respective indications were down 4.3%, 7%, and 2.5% for the session.

ING found on Nov. 20 that metals selling outpaced physical weakness. Copper had dropped more than 8% and gold about 9% during the week, even as physical markets remained tight. The bank attributed part of the decline to investors reducing bullish positions.

Brandt had raised concerns about gold before his broader deflation forecast. He cautioned in October that gold’s entire earlier advance from 2025 could disappear if its decline continued. That warning concerned the metal’s price; his Nov. 20 remarks extended to financial and raw material markets.

Consumer Prices Still Rose in October

Deflation would require a sustained decline in consumer prices across the economy. If an account pays 2% interest while prices fall 1%, then its purchasing power increases by roughly 3%. Brandt’s prediction depends on falling market prices being followed by broader declines in the prices consumers pay.

The Bureau of Labor Statistics reported Nov. 10 that consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, following a 0.6% increase in September. The October reading measured household costs before the latest market declines and remained above the threshold for deflation.

The 10-year breakeven inflation rate, a bond-market gauge of average inflation expected over the next decade, stood at 2.16% on Nov. 19. That measure reflects expectations over 10 years and can coexist with shorter periods of falling prices.

Bitcoin’s price decline alone does not show that consumer prices are falling. Recent bitcoin price swings during inflation show how its value can diverge from changes in the cost of living. The next U.S. consumer-price report, covering November, is scheduled for Dec. 10.

title: SEC Freezes Assets in $560 Million Crypto Trading Ponzi Scheme
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

SEC Freezes Assets in $560 Million Crypto Trading Ponzi Scheme
The SEC obtained an asset freeze against Backward Hat Capital and its founders, alleging a $560 million Ponzi scheme sold as AI-driven FX trading funded through crypto. Prosecutors and the CFTC filed parallel cases.
Thi...
content:
The Securities and Exchange Commission has frozen the assets of Indianapolis-based Backward Hat Capital and its two co-founders, saying the firm ran a $560 million Ponzi scheme that told investors their money would be turned into crypto and used for AI-driven currency trading.

The agency said Backward Hat, co-founders Phillip Williams and Devin Johnson, Johnson’s firm Traders Point Capital and Joseph Anderson raised the money from more than 2,000 investors starting in July 2022. A federal court granted a temporary restraining order, an asset freeze and expedited discovery to halt what the SEC called an ongoing scheme.

Federal prosecutors in New York and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission brought parallel cases. The SEC and CFTC suits were filed in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Indiana, and the CFTC said the court has appointed Kevin B. Duff as temporary receiver to take control of the companies and the individual defendants’ assets.

The pitch: crypto, AI and 6% a month

According to the SEC’s complaint, Williams and Johnson sold limited partnership interests in private funds through a network of promoters, including to Williams’s former investment advisory clients. They promised a proprietary, “AI-driven” algorithm that supposedly returned at least 6% every month by trading foreign exchange.

Investor money, the pitch went, would first be converted into a crypto asset and then used for that arbitrage. The complaint does not name bitcoin as the asset. It says about $109 million of the roughly $210 million raised from July 2022 to September 2025 was sent to the fund’s Coinbase account and converted.

Of that, more than $56 million went to personal crypto accounts held by Williams, Johnson and a relief defendant, according to the complaint. About $40 million ended up on three platforms where some of it was used to trade other crypto assets, but little to no money was used to trade FX. After October 2025, the scheme raised about $350 million, and none of it was sent to Coinbase.

Where the money went

The SEC said the defendants made more than $250 million in Ponzi payments to earlier investors and moved more than $220 million to themselves. The money paid for exotic cars, expensive homes, private air travel and other businesses they owned, and helped feed Johnson’s gambling. Promoters took more than $50 million.

Anderson is accused of producing fake financial reports, including at least two “audit reports” and a “quality of earnings” report from a supposedly independent firm. The SEC said the documents falsely claimed the returns had been verified against bank and brokerage records. It said Anderson did no audit work, was not independent and had a financial stake in the scheme.

Prosecutors in Manhattan charged Williams and Johnson with securities fraud, conspiracy to commit wire fraud and conspiracy to commit securities fraud. The FBI arrested Williams in Kokomo, Indiana, and Johnson in Gilbert, Arizona, on Wednesday. Prosecutors put the total raised at more than $600 million.

“As alleged, Phillip Patrick Williams and Devin Allen Johnson promised to use investor funds for profitable foreign exchange currency trading,” said U.S. Attorney Jamie McDonald. “Williams and Johnson instead stole hundreds of millions of dollars from their investors for personal expenses and to pay off earlier investors in a Ponzi-like fashion.”

Regulators’ latest crypto fraud cases

The CFTC put the Ponzi at more than $550 million from at least 2,100 participants and said defendants kept soliciting money through at least October 2026. Its complaint seeks restitution, disgorgement, civil penalties, trading bans and a permanent injunction. The SEC is seeking injunctions, disgorgement and civil penalties.

The case follows other recent enforcement actions tied to crypto-branded fraud. The SEC charged two companies in a $130 million crypto trading scheme last month, and New York sought a $1.37 billion judgment against the operators of the NovaTech Ponzi scheme. In August, the CFTC charged Goliath Ventures with a $400 million bitcoin fraud.

Anne McKinley, acting associate director of the SEC’s Chicago Regional Office, said the promise of “a low-risk, high rate of return on a purportedly complex investment should make all potential investors stop and think before investing their money.”

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Sky Protocol sees $2 billion in stablecoin withdrawals, disputes illicit fund claims
summary: Sky says its USDS stablecoin held its $1 value despite more than $2 billion in withdrawals, as it disputes a report linking the protocol to illicit activity.
content:
Sky Protocol processed more than $2 billion in stablecoin redemptions on Thursday, the same day a CoinDesk investigation linked $518 million in transactions through the protocol to illicit activity.

The withdrawals involved users exchanging Sky’s USDS stablecoin for Circle’s USDC through its Peg Stability Module (PSM), a system that allows users to swap the tokens at a fixed rate.

Sky, which has a total value locked (TVL) of $2.3 billion, said on Friday in a statement that USDS maintained its $1 peg throughout the withdrawals. According to the protocol, the amount of USDC held in the PSM never fell below $800 million and had climbed back above $1.1 billion by Friday.

Sky also challenged the investigation, pointing to a review by Block Analitica, which notably serves as a risk adviser to the Sky ecosystem.

The withdrawals came amid concerns raised by the investigation that Circle could freeze USDC held by Sky, potentially making it harder for users to redeem their stablecoins.

Related: Circle freezes $12.6M of USDC linked to privacy protocol Zama

Sky disputes findings on illicit transactions

CoinDesk’s Nov. 19 report looked at research by blockchain analytics firm Inca Digital, which identified $518 million in transactions involving wallets linked to hackers, sanctioned entities, and other threat actors over a span of five years.

Of that amount, around $101.9 million was linked to North Korean actors, including wallets connected to the February 2025 Bybit hack.

Meanwhile, Block Analitica disputed some parts of the investigation, saying that the $518 million represented less than 0.06% of the more than $960 billion processed through Sky’s peg stability modules.

The firm said about two-thirds of the flagged activity occurred between 2021 and mid-2024 – before Sky introduced its newer LitePSM system.

Block Analitica also questioned the reported links to North Korean threat actors, stating that some wallets were several transactions removed from known addresses and may have belonged to unrelated users.

The firm added that most of the flagged transactions passed through trading services such as 1inch, ParaSwap and MetaMask Swaps, which automatically choose where to route trades.

Sky says reserves remain strong despite withdrawals

The large withdrawals also came amid a sharp drop in the number of USDS tokens in circulation. The supply fell nearly 40% in one day to about 3.2 billion tokens, according to DefiLlama data. However, the stablecoin maintained its $1 value despite the decline.

CoinDesk reported that a wallet linked to crypto exchange Poloniex accounted for a large share of the withdrawals, although it wasn’t clear whether the exchange itself was behind the transactions.

The combined circulating supply of Sky’s USDS and DAI stablecoins fell to $6.11 billion as of Nov. 20, down 37.8% over the past 30 days. Source: Sky Ecosystem Financial Insights

Sky said it held about $9.3 billion in assets backing its stablecoins as of Friday, compared with around $6.11 billion in USDS and DAI in circulation, according to its financial dashboard. The dashboard also showed about $93 million in reserves to help cover potential losses.

Cointelegraph reached out to the Sky Frontier Foundation for comment but had not received a response by publication.

title: Bitcoin Price Crashes Below $59K as Crypto Liquidations Top $1.5B
summary: Bitcoin dropped below $59,000 on Friday, hitting a multi-month low of $58,701 and extending a steep November downturn that leaves the cryptocurrency down over 30% year-to-date. Bitcoin Plunges Below $59,000 Amid Broad Crypto Market Rout Bitcoin’s price plunged below $59,000 on Friday as the November...
content:
Bitcoin dropped below $59,000 on Friday, hitting a multi-month low of $58,701 and extending a steep November downturn that leaves the cryptocurrency down over 30% year-to-date.

Key Takeaways

  • Bitcoin fell below $59,000 on Friday, extending its year-to-date decline to over 30%.
  • The sell-off triggered $1.53 billion in crypto liquidations as Nvidia and AMD plunged alongside Anthropic.
  • Wintermute warns bitcoin must reclaim $68,000 with fresh ETF inflows before a December Fed rate hike.

Bitcoin Plunges Below $59,000 Amid Broad Crypto Market Rout

Bitcoin’s price plunged below $59,000 on Friday as the November cryptocurrency market rout showed no signs of letting up. The plunge came just days after crypto market maker Wintermute warned that bitcoin’s bear market was not over and flagged the risk of a further slide into the $50,000 range.

Bitstamp data shows bitcoin briefly dropped to $58,701, a level last seen in early July, when a bearish trend threatened to push the price toward $50,000. Earlier Friday, however, bitcoin appeared to be holding comfortably above $61,000, with $62,000 acting as its immediate resistance level.

Between 11 a.m. and noon EST, bitcoin shed nearly $3,000 amid heightened selling pressure and a lack of buyers. Although a relief rally briefly lifted the price above $59,300, the cryptocurrency was still down approximately 5% over 24 hours and more than 13% over seven days.

After narrowing its year-to-date losses to single digits by the end of September, bitcoin has steadily declined since the beginning of October. The latest sell-off leaves the cryptocurrency down more than 30% since Jan. 1.

Meanwhile, bitcoin’s sharp decline was particularly devastating for traders betting on higher prices. According to Coinglass data, the price collapse wiped out more than $220 million in leveraged long positions in just one hour, compared with less than $10 million in short positions.

Over 24 hours, bitcoin liquidations exceeded $543 million, including more than $494 million in long positions. With most major altcoins mirroring bitcoin’s decline, long liquidations across the broader cryptocurrency market surpassed $1.38 billion over 24 hours, while short liquidations totaled approximately $142 million—a total of $1.53 billion in liquidations across the market.

AI Stock Sell-Off and Anthropic IPO Slump Spill Into Crypto

In its Nov. 16 market update, Wintermute argued that bitcoin’s recent rebounds were primarily driven by short covering rather than fresh spot buying. Without renewed demand from spot bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs), which have recorded roughly $1.9 billion in net outflows in 2026, and corporate bitcoin treasury companies, the prospects for a sustained recovery remain slim.

Wintermute said bitcoin would need to reclaim $68,000 on a sustained basis, accompanied by a clear return to net spot ETF inflows, before the market maker would reconsider its bearish outlook.

The cryptocurrency market sell-off came on the heels of Anthropic’s record-breaking initial public offering (IPO), which raised more than $81 billion. However, the blockbuster listing failed to revive investor confidence in technology stocks, which have been battered by mounting concerns over artificial intelligence valuations, the profitability of massive AI infrastructure investments and the prospect of further U.S. interest rate hikes.

The pressure intensified Friday as Anthropic shares plunged almost 13% following their trading debut, while semiconductor stocks extended their losses. Nvidia fell approximately 7% in morning trading, while Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) dropped nearly 12%. Broadcom, Marvell Technology, and Micron Technology each shed more than 9%, underscoring the scale of the sell-off in companies closely tied to the AI boom.

The rout also reflected growing doubts about whether the billions of dollars being poured into AI infrastructure will generate sufficient returns to justify elevated technology stock valuations. Nvidia’s recent leadership upheaval, regulatory uncertainty following the U.S. midterm elections and concerns about higher borrowing costs have further undermined investor confidence.

Hawkish Fed Signals Push Equities and Risk Assets Lower

Adding to the pressure, hawkish signals from Federal Reserve officials have reinforced expectations of another interest rate hike in December. Higher borrowing costs typically weigh on growth-oriented technology companies by reducing the present value of their expected future earnings and making speculative investments less attractive.

The resulting sell-off pushed the Nasdaq down approximately 3.5% on Friday, while the broader S&P 500 fell 2%. The S&P 500 was heading toward its seventh consecutive losing session, while the Nasdaq briefly slipped into negative territory for the year. The simultaneous decline in bitcoin, technology stocks, and other risk-sensitive assets suggests that investors are increasingly reducing exposure to speculative investments amid mounting uncertainty over valuations, monetary policy, and economic growth.

title: Anthropic Stock Price Today: ANT Falls 8% as $500B US Tech Sell-Off Hits AI Stocks
summary: Anthropic shares came under renewed selling pressure on Friday as a broader technology market downturn erased much of the optimism surrounding the company's record-breaking Nasdaq debut.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: ANT

Anthropic shares came under renewed selling pressure on Friday as a broader technology market downturn erased much of the optimism surrounding the company's record-breaking Nasdaq debut.

ANT declined approximately 8% in the latest market snapshot, while semiconductor and artificial intelligence stocks also recorded steep losses. The pullback followed a turbulent first trading session on November 19, when Anthropic briefly reached a $2 trillion market valuation before retreating from its opening gains.

ANT Stock Price Retreats After Strong IPO Debut

Anthropic (ANT) shares faced a sharp correction on November 20, extending the volatility that followed their highly anticipated stock market debut. The company began trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on November 19 at an initial public offering (IPO) price of $83 per share.

Anthropic Stock (ANT) price chart. Source: @SantimentData/X

Investor demand initially pushed the stock considerably higher. ANT opened at $111.50, representing a 34% premium to its IPO price, and briefly reached a valuation of approximately $2 trillion. However, the initial buying momentum weakened throughout the session, leaving shares at $97.17 at Thursday’s close, still approximately 17% above the offering price.

The following day’s decline reflected growing caution among investors. Reuters reported ANT trading near $88.24 on Friday, approximately 9% below its previous close. The pullback erased a substantial portion of its first-session gains, although the shares remained above their original IPO price.

The scale of Anthropic’s listing also attracted attention. The company initially raised approximately $81.3 billion through its offering. Following the full exercise of the underwriters’ additional share purchase option, Anthropic disclosed that gross IPO proceeds had reached approximately $93.5 billion. A separate $26 billion private placement brought the combined proceeds from both transactions to approximately $119.5 billion.

The opening-day performance initially demonstrated strong demand for exposure to the AI industry. However, the subsequent correction suggests that investors remain selective about valuations, even when a company attracts substantial interest during its public debut.

$500B US Tech Sell-Off Weighs on AI Stocks

Anthropic’s declining share price coincided with an aggressive sell-off across US technology stocks. According to Coin Bureau’s November 20 market update, approximately $500 billion in market capitalization disappeared from US equities within minutes of the opening bell.

US markets suffered a sharp selloff on November 20, wiping out $500 billion in market value as tech and AI stocks tumbled, while the Nasdaq 100 fell 1.58%. Source: @coinbureau/X

ANT featured among the weakest-performing technology stocks in the update, falling 8.01%. Semiconductor companies also recorded substantial losses, highlighting the extent of the selling pressure across the AI infrastructure sector.

SanDisk declined 8.07%, while Western Digital lost 6.80%. Arm Holdings dropped 6.41%, followed by Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) at 6.32%, Micron Technology at 6.06%, Marvell Technology at 5.97%, and Riot Platforms at 5.30%.

The weakness extended beyond smaller technology companies. Nvidia, Alphabet, and Microsoft also traded lower, with losses of 3.30%, 3.46%, and 1.97%, respectively, in the market snapshot.

The Nasdaq 100 was down 1.58% in the reported snapshot, reflecting renewed pressure on companies closely associated with AI development and semiconductor manufacturing.

Concerns surrounding the sustainability of AI investment have increasingly influenced market sentiment. Investors are questioning whether the enormous capital commitments toward data centers, computing infrastructure, and advanced semiconductor technology can generate sufficient returns.

The broader financial environment has added another layer of uncertainty. Expectations of higher interest rates, rising infrastructure costs, and concerns about AI company valuations have encouraged investors to reassess exposure to growth-oriented technology stocks.

David Miller, chief investment officer at Catalyst Funds, described the changing investment outlook in comments reported by Reuters: “Investors still believe in AI but are becoming more selective about what they will pay for that growth.”

That distinction is important for Anthropic. Its strong IPO demonstrated substantial interest in the company’s business, but the subsequent share-price decline indicates that investor enthusiasm does not necessarily translate into sustained buying pressure across the wider AI sector.

Tokenized Anthropic Shares Draw Attention in Crypto Markets

Anthropic’s public listing also generated significant activity across cryptocurrency platforms, where tokenized securities and derivatives provided additional ways to gain exposure to the company.

Santiment reported a substantial increase in social volume and social dominance surrounding Anthropic tokenization discussions on November 19. Its charts showed simultaneous increases in bullish and bearish mentions, indicating heightened market attention and divided sentiment following the IPO.

Anthropic’s ANT token surged following its $81.3 billion IPO debut before retreating sharply while expanding across multiple blockchains and DeFi platforms. Source: Santiment Intelligence via X

The growing discussion reflects the expansion of tokenized equity products across blockchain networks and decentralized finance platforms. These products allow users to access blockchain-based representations of traditional financial assets, although their structure, trading conditions, and associated risks can differ from those of the underlying shares.

A Glassnode chart also highlighted activity in pre-IPO Anthropic perpetual futures. These contracts reportedly implied valuations between $1.7 trillion and $1.85 trillion during much of the listing week before climbing toward $2 trillion shortly before the Nasdaq debut.

The chart suggests that 24/7 crypto derivatives markets identified Anthropic’s IPO as undervalued, providing more timely pricing signals than traditional banker-set valuations. Source: Glassnode via X

The comparison illustrates how cryptocurrency derivatives markets can reflect changing expectations outside conventional US trading hours. However, futures-based valuations represent trading expectations rather than official company valuations or guaranteed future share prices.

Meanwhile, Binance Wallet announced compensation arrangements for participants in its Anthropic IPO xStocks campaign after encountering allocation problems beyond its control.

The platform confirmed that participating users would receive full refunds of their committed USDC, alongside a proportional distribution of the available tokenized Anthropic shares. Eligible participants were also set to receive an additional $1 million allocation of bStocks Anthropic tokens, identified by the ticker ANTB.

The announcement highlighted continued demand for blockchain-based access to newly listed companies. It also demonstrated the operational challenges that can emerge when subscription demand exceeds the available allocation of an IPO-linked tokenized product.

Overall, Anthropic’s first two trading sessions have exposed a gap between strong initial demand for its shares and the broader market’s willingness to maintain higher valuations for AI companies. The stock’s next direction will depend partly on how investors assess its growth prospects, spending commitments, and ability to sustain confidence as a publicly traded company.

title: Bitcoin falls below $60K for first time since July amid broader market selloff
summary: Bitcoin fell nearly 6% as US stocks declined, with the Nasdaq dropping more than 2% and Anthropic shares losing almost 10%.
content:
Bitcoin fell below $60,000 on Friday for the first time since July, extending its recent losses amid a broader selloff in technology stocks and other risk assets.

Bitcoin (BTC) had fallen to $58,811 before recovering slightly to trade around $59,503, down 5.6% over the past 24 hours as of 16:52 UTC on Friday, according to CoinGecko data. The cryptocurrency has fallen 13.8% over the past week and nearly 30% over the past month.

Source: CoinGecko

The decline came amid a broader selloff in US equities. The Nasdaq Composite closed down 5.28% at 22,617.73, while the S&P 500 fell 3.69% to 6,910.77 on Friday, according to Yahoo Finance.

Shares of Anthropic (ANT), which made its Nasdaq debut on Thursday, closed down 8.50% at $88.91 amid concerns over valuations and spending in the artificial intelligence sector.

US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds recorded $582.3 million in net outflows on Thursday, up from $306.5 million the previous day, according to Farside Investors. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) accounted for $541.1 million of Thursday’s withdrawals.

AI selloff drives Bitcoin weakness, CoinShares says

Bitcoin’s decline appears to be driven more by the broader selloff in artificial intelligence stocks than by problems specific to the cryptocurrency market, according to James Butterfill, head of research at CoinShares.

Butterfill told Cointelegraph that Bitcoin has increasingly traded alongside other liquidity-sensitive growth assets, with deteriorating sentiment toward AI stocks spilling into crypto as investors reduce risk. The prospect of interest rates remaining elevated has made the broader selloff more severe, he added.

The Federal Reserve held its benchmark interest rate at 3.75% to 4.00% in October, following a quarter-point increase in September. Traders on Polymarket were pricing in a 94% chance of another rate hike by the Fed’s next policy decision on Dec. 9, as of 17:19 UTC on Friday.

Polymarket traders price in 94% chance of another Fed rate hike in 2026. Source: Polymarket

Despite Bitcoin falling below $60,000, Butterfill said the decline has not fundamentally changed his medium-term outlook.

We have been expecting Bitcoin to trade broadly between $60,000 and $90,000 until there is a meaningful change in liquidity or monetary policy, so a temporary move below the bottom of that range is uncomfortable rather than thesis-changing.

Butterfill said Bitcoin could face further short-term losses if the AI selloff deepens, but should benefit relatively quickly if technology stocks stabilize.

Alexander Blume, founder and CEO of digital asset investment firm Two Prime, told Cointelegraph that macroeconomic instability, interest rates, inflation and a lack of Bitcoin-specific catalysts were contributing to the decline.

However, Blume suggested that selling pressure may be nearing an end.

That being said, I think sellers and leverage liquidations are largely exhausted and would not be surprised for BTC to find a bottom soon.

title: Researchers Publish Security Analysis of Bitcoin’s Post-Quantum SHRINCS Proposal
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Researchers Publish Security Analysis of Bitcoin’s Post-Quantum SHRINCS Proposal
Blockstream researchers published a 131-page security analysis of SHRINCS, a hash-based post-quantum signature scheme for Bitcoin, and are asking the community to review it for flaws.
This post Researc...
content:
Several researchers have published a 131-page security analysis of SHRINCS, a proposed post-quantum signature scheme for Bitcoin, and are asking the wider community to look for flaws in it. Researcher Mikhail Kudinov announced the first version Thursday in a thread on X, saying the paper reduces SHRINCS’ security to the properties of its underlying hash function.

The analysis, dated Nov. 18, estimates classical security of 121.4 to 122.7 bits for SHRINCS, though those figures rest on assumptions that include three unproven conjectures. Kudinov said the work is not finished. The team is still working on a new analysis of a property called SM-DSPR, whose bound has so far been conjectured, and on tightening a reprogramming step and improving a bound against quantum attackers.

How SHRINCS works

SHRINCS is a hash-based scheme, meaning its security rests on hash functions rather than the elliptic curve math behind today’s Bitcoin signatures. It places two designs under one key: a stateful part built on FXMSS with WOTS+C, and a stateless fallback built on SLH-DSA. Because both use the same hash function, Kudinov said, the proof has to cover both.

Signature size is the main cost. Under the draft proposal, stateful SHRINCS signatures run from 548 to 4,619 bytes, while the stateless fallback is 5,777 bytes. Schnorr signatures on Bitcoin today are 64 bytes, and ECDSA signatures typically come in around 71. Signatures take up scarce block space, so larger ones mean fewer transactions per block.

The risk of a stateful signature

The compact stateful path carries a danger. It relies on one-time keys, and if a wallet accidentally reuses one, an attacker can forge a signature for that address and steal the funds. Wallet software therefore has to track the state of every key. The stateless path avoids the problem, but at a much larger size.

Jonas Nick, Blockstream’s director of research, told Isabel Foxen Duke, head of the MARA Foundation, on MARA Foundation TV that wallets must automatically fall back to the stateless path whenever a state counter could be compromised. “It needs to be impossible for the user to behave in a way that this catastrophic event happens,” he said. “Wallet developers need to deal with this stateful component correctly.”

Nick also warned that heavy use of the larger signatures would weigh on the network. “We don’t know what the fee market will look like once we have these very big signatures,” he said. “And it’s not just the fee market, it’s also just fewer transactions fit into a block, meaning fewer people can use Bitcoin. And I think this changes the value proposition of Bitcoin.”

Researchers ask for review

The authors are clear that the analysis needs scrutiny. Kudinov said it has not been sufficiently peer reviewed, and the project’s GitHub repository warns that the documents may contain errors and should not be the sole basis for deploying SHRINCS. “We tried to be careful, but a proof of this size can have mistakes,” he wrote, asking readers to open an issue if they find one.

The team also produced two results that are not specific to SHRINCS: a classical bound for a property called ITSR without reprogramming, and a quadratic quantum bound for undetectability. Kudinov said they also apply to SPHINCS+ and SLH-DSA, the hash-based schemes SHRINCS borrows from, and that they were published as separate papers.

The SHRINCS work lands as quantum risk climbs the agenda. A global securities regulators’ group this week warned that moving blockchains to quantum-resistant cryptography may be especially hard, and researchers recently built a post-quantum defense for the Lightning Network after Bitcoin’s first quantum-safe transaction was shown without a fork.

The draft Bitcoin Improvement Proposal for SHRINCS is also open for comment. “We need all the possible feedback — engineers, cryptographers, protocol developers,” Kudinov, a post-quantum cryptography researcher at Blockstream, said of it. “There are a lot of things to check, test, complain about, or praise.”

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

  • Deribit trading platform will serve as the new offering’s trading infrastructure and liquidity.

Coinbase continues to delve deeper into the crypto derivatives sector and introduces options trading to eligible customers in certain markets globally, excluding the United States.

The rollout gives retail traders direct access to Deribit-powered options through Coinbase, adding another major derivatives product alongside perpetual futures and spot trading.

The option you’ve been waiting for: crypto options.

Define your risk, trade volatility and express your view on the market all in one world-class trading experience.

Powered by Deribit’s deep global liquidity, available now on Coinbase. https://t.co/Th1cHWZ7g3

— Coinbase 🛡️ (@coinbase) November 19, 2026

  • Coinbase Adds Six Crypto Options Markets
    • Combo Orders Bring Multi-Leg Strategies to Coinbase
  • Deribit Powers Coinbase’s Options
  • US Crypto Options Access Is Next

Coinbase Adds Six Crypto Options Markets

Coinbase currently has offerings related to Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, Avalanche, Hyperliquid and XRP.

The contracts are linear options with settleable price in USDC and executed on Deribit’s infrastructure. Call or put options give users the flexibility to manage downside risk, trade volatility and create more advanced strategies, depending on their market opinion.

Some Exchange members may offer options trading outside the United States in their applicable regions. To enter Coinbase’s offering in the crypto spaces called Global Derivatives, users must first have an open spot account.

Combo Orders Bring Multi-Leg Strategies to Coinbase

This includes a number of combo orders, which allow users to place multiple legs of an option contract simultaneously from Coinbase Advanced. A trader can for instance go long a call, but short the same month call at a higher strike price.

Some linear selections are available on BTC, ETH, SOL and XRP with combo structures settled and priced in USDC. The availability of assets depends on the strike, expiring and user location.

For more advanced traders, this provides a tool to help determine risk and potential returns prior to entering a trade, not just by spot or perpetual trades.

Deribit Powers Coinbase’s Options

Coinbase’s inclusion of Deribit into its derivatives platform comes as the launch. Coinbase integrated all of its international derivatives operations onto its platform Deribit on Oct. 1, forming a unified platform to centralize its liquidity, risk infrastructure and real-time matching engine.

The assets and perpetual futures are powered by the underlying infrastructure provided by Coinbase through Deribit, the company said.

The company had indicated that the integration was to be part of a broader push to create one platform that spans the spot, futures, perpetuals and options space. In addition, Coinbase Pro will also be brought back as a professional trading platform on these markets.

Read More: Coinbase Launches AI Agent Sign-Ups for Crypto Trading With Built-In Safety Limits

US Crypto Options Access Is Next

Brian Armstrong, CEO of Coinbase, announced that crypto options are now available for all non-US customers and will be introduced to its US customers via Coinbase Pro. Coinbase has yet to set a retail launch date for the United States.

Crypto options are now live for non-US users!

And are also coming to the US soon with Coinbase Pro 👀

— Brian Armstrong (@brian_armstrong) November 19, 2026

There, Coinbase Prime and Coinbase Financial Markets will provide eligible US institutional clients with global crypto derivatives services, where orders are directed to Deribit via a regulated brokerage mechanism.

Coinbase’s inclusion of options represents another substantial addition to its trading suite and provides direct exposure for Coinbase’s users to Deribit’s famed crypto options platform.
