  • Global retail traders now have access to one of the market's most anticipated artificial intelligence listings on MT5 and Elev8Trader, following its launch on 19 November 2026

Elev8, a global Contracts for Difference (CFD) broker, announced it has added Anthropic, PBC (Nasdaq: ANT), a company behind the Claude AI platform, to its tradable asset lineup under the ticker symbol ANT.NAS, effective 19 November 2026. The launch follows Anthropic's record-setting initial public offering (IPO) on Nasdaq. The ANT.NAS CFD is now available as a permanent addition across both MetaTrader 5 (MT5) and Elev8Trader.

A critical moment for the AI trade

Over the past two years, the AI trade has become a central theme across global stock markets. Heavy investment in AI-related stocks and industries has reshaped global markets, making Anthropic's public debut the largest stock-market listing on record and a major milestone of 2026 for both the technology sector and the global AI trade.

Anthropic entered the public market after increasing its share sale by 19% to 980 million shares and pricing the IPO at $83 per share—above its initial $70 to $78 range. According to Reuters, the offering raised a record $81.3 billion (part of a $107.3 billion total deal including a $26 billion private placement), with the company achieving a fully diluted valuation of about $2 trillion in its Nasdaq debut and surpassing SpaceX's previous IPO record.

On its first day of trading, shares opened at $111.50 (up 34% from the IPO price) before paring gains to close at $97.17, up 17%. Despite broader market debate over AI spending and valuations, Anthropic is backed by strong global investor demand. The listing of this first publicly traded frontier AI company gives traders a direct benchmark for global AI performance.

Capturing peak post-IPO momentum and volatility

Elev8 is committed to giving its clients timely access to the world's most talked-about and influential public companies. By launching ANT.NAS on 19 November, just hours after its Nasdaq debut, Elev8 enables traders to trade both the stock's longer-term market moves and the most active period in the first two to four weeks after listing (when post-IPO volatility is usually at its highest).

Historical market data shows that newly listed mega-cap companies frequently see sharp up-and-down price swings before stabilising over 6 to 18 months. Elev8 wants its clients to have the opportunity to trade this initial price action as early as possible.

Why post-IPO volatility is elevated

Post-IPO volatility is often driven by market uncertainty, tight supply of shares, and early investor hype. For Anthropic, ongoing market debate around heavy AI infrastructure spending and growing industry competition adds to these price swings. With no prior public trading history, investors often struggle to agree on fair value, while a limited supply of freely traded shares means routine trades can cause large price moves. Momentum trading often triggers a 'first-day pop' followed by a pullback, and upcoming earnings reports and business milestones can create new waves of price adjustments.

Elev8’s key trading specifications for Anthropic, PBC

  • Underlying listing: Nasdaq : ANT

  • Instrument/Symbol: Anthropic, PBC (ANT.NAS)

  • Launch date: 19 November 2026 (permanent addition)

  • Supported platforms: MetaTrader 5 (MT5) and Elev8Trader

  • Trading capabilities: long and short CFD positions with built-in risk-management tools.

Disclaimer: This article does not contain or constitute investment advice or recommendations and does not consider your investment objectives, financial situation, or needs. Any actions taken based on this content are at your sole discretion and risk—Elev8 does not accept any liability for any resulting losses or consequences.

Operating under licences from Mauritius and Seychelles, Elev8 provides traders with the tools to help spot and capture more market opportunities. The broker received the 'Best Trading Experience Broker 2026' and the 'Best Trading Platform Provider 2026' awards from FxDailyInfo.

One of Elev8's key features is Space, an analytics hub within the Elev8Trader platform that helps traders expand their market horizons. With its personalised feed, daily expert analytics, and community content, Space facilitates faster access to information and market data.

MEXC futures bonuses can be used for eligible USDT-M futures trading. The bonus can help cover trading fees, funding fees, realized losses, and, in some cases, margin after available USDT is insufficient.

But obviously, there is no way to simply withdraw the futures bonus itself as cash. The bonus remains promotional credit only, and eligible profit generated through it can be withdrawn, which is a very important difference.

How to Apply the MEXC Referral Code (mexc-bestbonus) When Opening a New Trading Account?

To apply the referral code when opening a new account, you need to enter “mexc-bestbonus” during MEXC registration, then complete KYC, make the required deposit, and meet the futures trading volume tasks to qualify for the full sign-up bonus linked to the invite code.

Step 1: Create an Account With Our Referral Code

First, you need to go to the official MEXC website and click “Sign Up”. Enter your email address or phone number, create a password, and open the referral code field.

Next, enter “mexc-bestbonus” exactly as shown. You know that referral codes are case-sensitive, so check the spelling before you finish registration. After that, complete the email or phone verification code and create your account. Also, it is better to add the referral code during account registration because the code connects your new account with the referral offer from the start.

Step 2: Complete KYC Verification

Next, log in to your MEXC account and go to the “Profile” section, then “Identification”. You can then start primary or advanced KYC verification.

Step 3: Deposit Funds

You need to add funds to your MEXC account after KYC. Go to “Wallets”, then “Deposit,” and choose the cryptocurrency you want to transfer, such as USDT.

Then, select the correct blockchain network and copy your MEXC deposit address. The network you choose on MEXC must match the network used by the sending wallet or exchange. A wrong network will definitely result in lost funds. MEXC also supports several fiat purchase methods as well, although payment options can vary by country. You can check that out too.

Now, once your account has enough funds, go to “Futures” from the main navigation menu. You can choose USDT-M, USDC-M, or Coin-M Futures. Next, choose a trading pair, set your order type, enter the amount, and open your position. These tools can also suit experienced traders who want more flexibility with futures strategies. MEXC also runs monthly futures competitions with large prize pools.

Finally, return to “Rewards Hub” after you complete tasks required by the promotion. Well, task progress can take up to around 30 minutes to update, and once the task shows as completed, click the available “Claim” button; in some campaigns, eligible spot trades can count toward certain bonus tasks.

Here, remember, MEXC futures bonuses cannot normally be withdrawn directly. You can use them for futures margin, trading fees, funding fees, or even sometimes trading losses, while profits made from eligible bonus-funded trades may be withdrawn.

You can also go directly to the MEXC referral program section**.** Your personal code and link show up right there automatically, and you can use the Invite Friends feature to share them with eligible new users to receive referral rewards when they meet the required conditions. Also, some task-based vouchers exist separately too, covering a fixed dollar amount of fees for a limited stretch of time after you claim them.

A MEXC New User Sign-Up Bonus is a group of welcome rewards offered to eligible users after they create a new account and complete selected tasks.

As discussed above, MEXC currently offers new-user rewards worth up to 10,000 USDT. But again, this does not mean every new account receives 10,000 USDT immediately. title: Lithium Price Analysis as 2027 Supply Risks Clash With Weak Market Momentum
summary: Lithium Price Analysis is looking at how prices are affected as Zimbabwe's export ban has not budged in the market.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: Li

Lithium Price Analysis is looking at how prices are affected as Zimbabwe's export ban has not budged in the market.

Investors are not yet convinced that the market has hit a lasting low for lithium, as the rally is faltering to close in on recent price action.

Lithium’s rally is trying to prove that the market has hit an enduring bottom, but it is having trouble closing in on recent price action. Carbonate prices have rebounded to over 91,500 yuan per tonne, while the stock prices of companies in the lithium sector remain dropping.

China’s Carbonate Rebound Faces A Supply Overhang

The X market update has China’s lithium carbonate index at 91,520 yuan per tonne, up 1.71%. Battery-grade carbonate also rose by 1.33% to 91,600 yuan. This is an improvement, implying there is a return to buying after a period of weakness. The recovery is still relatively tiny compared to the previous drop in the market.

The long-term price structure reveals that lithium’s price has been rising rapidly since late 2025 and is expected to hit around 200,000 yuan per tonne around May. Source: Carlos Via X

However, prices turned down, making lower highs and lower lows during the remainder of the session. The latest recovery, then, is not a trend reversal but a big bounce in a downward pattern.

The proposed ban on concentrate exports from January 2027 in Zimbabwe is another possible supply disruption. But miners are pressing for delays, and lithium sulfate exports may go up with new processing capacity. This uncertainty makes it hard to imagine there is an immediate shortage of supply.

Prices Remain Under Pressure Despite Recent Stabilization

According to the latest data, the loss for the day was 0.54%, while the loss for the month was 10.80%. This is a sign that the overall weakness has not been overcome. Despite rising prices in recent sessions, the market is still far below the earlier high prices.

TradingEconomics’ chart indicates that lithium carbonate has pulled back from its peak in May and is heading back towards the 91,300 yuan level. Source: TradingEconomics

The downward trend indicates that traders are still pricing in the concerns of reduced supply availability and increased growth in demand. Zimbabwe’s export bans on concentrates may affect exports, but it’s unclear when and how the restrictions will be enforced. In the interim, China keeps importing lithium materials from other producing areas. As such, the expected supply shortfall has yet to offset inventory and consumption concerns.

Lithium Equities Signal Continued Investor Caution

The drop is also evidence that investors are still hesitant to invest in miners and battery companies, despite the carbonate rally. Market participants are not only considering current commodity gains but also future earnings and supply expansion and demand expectations, given the price weakness shown by the ETF.

Global X Lithium and Battery Tech ETF (LITR) fell by 0.92% to close at $55.06 on the TradingView chart. Source: TradingView

But its overall trend has been down after breaking below around $85 this year. The fund has been continuing to make lower highs and lower lows and has shown that the overall weakness across lithium-related equities continues.

title: A Feeling of Déjà Vu As Crypto Exchanges Fall Short in Anthropic’s IPO Tokenization
summary:
This year produced the two largest IPOs in history, SpaceX in June and Anthropic on Thursday. In both cases, crypto’s attempt to give retail investors tokenized access to hot IPOs ran into the same immovable constraint. Someone still has to secure the shares.
Major crypto platforms, including Binanc...
content:
2026-11-20T10:05:34.370+02:00

Friday, 20/11/2026 | 08:05 GMT by Adonis Adoni

  • Repeating the SpaceX IPO failure, Binance returned $500M in USDC after securing just 2,957 Anthropic tokens from xStocks, leaving eager retail investors empty-handed.
  • Meanwhile, Bitget bypassed xStocks to secure 153,774 shares directly, yet retail allocations remained vanishingly small, highlighting that supply remains the ultimate bottleneck.

This year produced the two largest IPOs in history, SpaceX in June and Anthropic on Thursday. In both cases, crypto’s attempt to give retail investors tokenized access to hot IPOs ran into the same immovable constraint. Someone still has to secure the shares.

Major crypto platforms, including Binance and Bitget, were forced to refund customers after failing to obtain enough of the underlying stock to meet tokenized-subscription demand.

London's trading industry is coming home!

High Demand, Scarce Shares

When Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei rang NASDAQ’s opening bell on November 19, the AI powerhouse began trading under ticker ANT at $111.50 per share, a swift 34% jump over its $83 IPO price.

That very day, Binance Wallet announced it would return all USDC locked in its Anthropic xStocks campaign. Run alongside xStocks, the tokenized-equity arm linked to Kraken’s parent company Payward, the campaign hit its 500 million USDC cap almost immediately before shutting down early on November 18.

Due to circumstances outside of our control, the allocation for the Anthropic xStocks IPO Campaign on Binance Wallet was not ideal. 🔸All participating users’ USDC will be fully returned from the relevant smart contract to their Binance Wallet. 🔸 An allocation totaling roughly 2,957 Anthropic tokenized stocks, will be airdropped pro rata, based on each user's share of the total subscription, to their Binance Wallet addresses at no cost. 🔸 In addition, $1,000,000 worth of bStocks Anthropic tokens (ANTB) will be airdropped to users who applied for a subscription, with a minimum of about 6 USDC worth guaranteed for each eligible participant, and the remainder distributed pro rata based on each user's share of the total subscription. Thank you for your patience and support. For more details, please refer to the announcement👇 https://t.co/kYf06cppeQ

— Binance Wallet (@BinanceWallet) November 19, 2026

Binance acquired a meager 2,957 tokenized shares. Rather than attempting a standard paid distribution with such tiny inventory, Binance chose to airdrop the tokens for free pro-rata to participants, fully refunding all locked USDC and tacking on $1 million in ANTB (its separate bStocks token) as compensation.

Binance Wallet cited unspecified "circumstances outside of our control" for the shortfall, admitting the tiny allocation was "not ideal." It nearly verbatim repeated Binance’s statement when its SpaceX tokenized offering collapsed back in June.

Echoes of the SpaceX Stumble

The parallels to the SpaceX fallout are hard to miss. During that launch, Binance Wallet, Bybit, Bitget Wallet and MEXC all had to pull their tokenized offerings after xStocks failed to secure enough underlying equity. Binance alone returned roughly $557 million in USDC to around 27,700 users without delivering any actual SpaceX exposure.

This time, though, at least one platform appeared to have learned a lesson about supply.

UPDATE: All the refund has been completed, as well as the rToken distribution. Please check your Bitget account accordingly and reach out to our support team if any queries. Thank you all for your patience.

— Bitget (@bitget) November 20, 2026

Bypassing xStocks completely, Bitget routed its Anthropic offering through Bitget IPO Prime, its proprietary real-world-asset launchpad. By securing 153,774 shares directly, Bitget actually fulfilled user requests instead of canceling the event outright.

Bybit and MEXC sidestepped the headache altogether, avoiding asset-backed tokenized IPO deals this round.

For their part, xStocks and Kraken did not publicly disclose how many shares they secured or what share of user requests they filled. In a November 19 statement, xStocks cited oversubscription of more than 9x and confirmed that it could fulfill only part of demand.

It is worth mentioning that these episodes also highlight regulatory boundaries, as platforms like xStocks explicitly block U.S. residents from participating.

Supply, Not Demand, Remains the Bottleneck

Ultimately, both mega-IPOs proved that retail appetite for tokenized pre-IPO access is massive, yet real-world equity sourcing remains a glaring weakness.

In the SpaceX campaign, a major failure point was xStocks, as Binance and its peers were not sourcing SpaceX shares themselves, but reselling an allocation that xStocks had promised to procure. When the supplier came up short, the reseller was inevitably left stranded.

Bitget’s experience, though, shows that even when a platform secures shares through its own channels, retail allocation can still be vanishingly small. A tokenized IPO product is only as valuable as the shares, or economic exposure, actually behind it.

title: Crypto business setup costs: how to compare a first-year budget
summary:
A founder comparing crypto business setup
proposals needs to know what the quoted price will deliver. One proposal may
cover company incorporation and documents. Another may include work on a
licence application. Both can leave banking, compliance systems and continuing
administration to be priced s...
content:
A founder comparing crypto business setup proposals needs to know what the quoted price will deliver. One proposal may cover company incorporation and documents. Another may include work on a licence application. Both can leave banking, compliance systems and continuing administration to be priced separately.

The first question is therefore what the business needs to operate in its intended markets. Once that is clear, the founder can compare the professional work, outside costs and ongoing commitments against the same scope.

Start with the services and customer markets

Describe what the business will actually do: exchange, transfers, custody, trading or providing a technology platform. Explain how money and crypto-assets move, who controls assets or private keys, and which entities sign the customer contracts. List the countries where customers will be based and where the business plans to market its services.

A founder comparing Panama and Costa Rica, for example, needs a written assessment of the proposed activities and customer markets before selecting a company structure. The assessment should identify the applicable requirements and explain the limits of the proposed arrangement. Incorporation alone does not establish permission to provide every service in every customer market.

Founders researching VASP licensing costs should ask which part of the proposal concerns company formation, which concerns regulatory analysis and whether a licence, registration or authorisation application is actually included or required. Each deliverable needs a clear description.

What does the professional fee buy?

Fast Offshore Licenses gives an indicative range of US$5,000–10,000 for its support, depending on the services selected. The written proposal should specify the work covered and identify which official fees, third-party charges and continuing costs are included or payable separately.

A package may bring together incorporation, anti-money-laundering documents, assistance with account applications and a legal opinion on the proposed structure. Ask for the deliverable and responsible person for each item. A legal opinion should explain the facts and activities it assesses, the law it relies on and any limits to its conclusions. Account-opening assistance should state what the adviser will do and which decisions belong to the account provider.

title: CROO Launches CROO Skill, Opening Its AI Agent Network to Claude Code and Codex Users
summary: Santa Clara, California, 20th November 2026, Chainwire
content:
Skip to content

Santa Clara, California, 20th November 2026, Chainwire

Santa Clara, California, November 20th, 2026, Chainwire

CROO, a decentralized commerce network for AI agents, announced the launch of CROO Skill for Claude Code and Codex. With the skill installed, users can describe a task in plain language, have their assistant find agents that offer the service, and review a quote before placing an order. The assistant can retrieve the finished work and save it to the project directory.

AI agents can already write code, conduct research, and analyze markets. Selling that work requires a way for customers to find a service, agree on what it will deliver, verify the result, and pay the provider. Payment protocols such as x402 let software pay for individual requests. CROO connects those payments to a marketplace and an order process that people and agents can both use.

“AI agents are becoming a new kind of worker, but today most of them still can’t find customers, sign a deal or get paid on their own,” said Jisko, Co-founder and CEO of CROO. “CROO is building the network that lets them do that, openly, for any agent on any framework. With CROO Skill, the agent you already use becomes a gateway to thousands of specialist agents. We see this as the start of an economy where agents hire each other, and where a good agent is an asset its owner truly owns.”

Agent Discovery and Payment Process

Developers retain ownership of the agents they bring to CROO, whether those agents run locally, are hosted in the cloud, or are packaged as skills. A developer with a wallet tracker, for example, can list a transaction report as a paid service with a defined deliverable on the CROO Agent Store. Buyers can browse the marketplace or search by describing a task in Navigator. CROO Skill makes those listings discoverable when a user requests relevant work in Claude Code or Codex.

The CROO Agent Protocol (CAP) gives people and agents common rules for agreeing on order terms, holding payment in escrow, verifying delivery, and settling on-chain. Completed orders contribute to the provider’s reputation record.

From a request to a delivered service

A user asks Claude Code to find an agent that can run their social media accounts automatically. Once the assistant finds a matching service, it shows a service fee of 3 USDC, a network fee of 0.02 USDC, and the delivery window for the order. After the user approves the payment, the agent starts providing the service.

CROO Skill supports orders on both Base and BNB Chain. Base orders use CAP escrow and settle in USDC, a dollar-pegged stablecoin. On BNB Chain, orders are paid directly over x402 and settled through Binance B402. Before paying, users can review which files and task details will be shared with the provider. Every payment requires the user’s approval and is signed by the user’s own Binance Agentic Wallet, so CROO Skill never needs access to the wallet’s private keys.

Network activity and availability

As of early November 2026, CROO reported more than 4,000 agents, over 570,000 completed orders, more than 1 million on-chain transactions, and over $880,000 in cumulative settled volume across Base and BNB Chain. CROO has partnered with more than 20 developer communities across Asia, Africa, the Middle East, and Latin America.

Users can obtain CROO Skill from the official installation page. A limited-time onboarding campaign is available to users and developers at https://campaigns.croo.network/croo-skill.html. CROO is also developing CROO Exchange, a planned marketplace for agents with a track record of paid work.

About CROO

CROO is decentralized infrastructure for the AI agent economy. It onboards agents, whether local, hosted, or skills of general agents, into an A2A and H2A coordination network where they can be discovered, hired and paid on-chain, enabling owners to monetize autonomous work and unlock agent asset value. CROO is live on Base and BNB Chain. Learn more at croo.network and follow @CROONetwork on X.

title: How to Deposit Bitcoin at an Online Entertainment Platform
summary:
Depositing Bitcoin at an online entertainment platform means selecting Bitcoin in the cashier, copying the address or Lightning invoice it generates and approving the payment from a wallet or exchange
The post How to Deposit Bitcoin at an Online Entertainment Platform appeared first on CryptoNinjas.
content:
Depositing Bitcoin at an online entertainment platform means selecting Bitcoin in the cashier, copying the address or Lightning invoice it generates and approving the payment from a wallet or exchange account. A confirmed transaction can’t be reversed, so the network, address, minimum and fee need checking first. On-chain payments wait for confirmations, Lightning usually settles in seconds, and a deposit limit caps how much goes in.

  • Choosing a Crypto Wallet for Online Entertainment Platforms
  • On-Chain Bitcoin or the Lightning Network
  • Minimum Deposits on Bitcoin Entertainment Platforms
  • Copying the Bitcoin Address or Lightning Invoice
  • Bitcoin Transaction Fees and Sending the Deposit
  • How Long Does a Bitcoin Transaction Take?
  • What to Do When a Bitcoin Deposit Goes Wrong
    • Crypto Sent to the Wrong Network or Address
    • Bitcoin Transaction Unconfirmed or Pending
    • Expired Lightning Invoice
    • Deposit Confirmed but Not Credited
  • How to Spend Bitcoin Responsibly on Entertainment Platforms

Choosing a Crypto Wallet for Online Entertainment Platforms

A self-custody wallet is the simplest source for a platform deposit, because the user controls the keys rather than a third party. Exchanges sometimes block transfers to certain gaming platforms and restrict related activity in their terms, so a user sending from one should check those terms first.

The wallet has to support the route the platform uses, so paying over Lightning takes a Lightning-capable wallet. Platforms commonly screen incoming coins with blockchain analysis, and coins that have passed through a mixer can freeze the account until their origin is documented.

A self-custody wallet should have its seed phrase backed up offline before any funds arrive.

On-Chain Bitcoin or the Lightning Network

The cashier shows whether Bitcoin deposits run on-chain, over the Lightning Network or both, and the user’s wallet has to support the same route. A user trying one of the new Bitcoin entertainment platforms should check which route it offers rather than assume a newer site takes Lightning.

  • On-chain payments are recorded on the blockchain and credited after the confirmations the platform requires.
  • Lightning payments move through payment channels instead of waiting for a block, which usually makes them faster and cheaper.

Minimum Deposits on Bitcoin Entertainment Platforms

Bitcoin minimums on online entertainment platforms commonly fall between 0.0001 and 0.0005 BTC, about $6 to $32 at mid-November 2026 prices. The cashier shows the exact figure, which the arriving sum has to meet. An exchange that deducts its withdrawal fee can leave a deposit of exactly the minimum short, and one below it may not be credited.

Copying the Bitcoin Address or Lightning Invoice

The user selects Bitcoin and the route in the cashier, which then shows the deposit details as text or as a QR code. After pasting or scanning, the user compares the whole string with the cashier, not just the first and last characters, because clipboard malware can swap a copied address for one an attacker controls. A cold crypto wallet with its own screen shows the destination and amount of an on-chain payment before signing, though it can’t confirm who the recipient is.

A Lightning invoice is a payment request rather than an address. It usually starts with “lnbc”, can carry a fixed amount and has an expiry time, so both deserve a look before paying.

Bitcoin Transaction Fees and Sending the Deposit

An on-chain network fee depends on the transaction’s size in virtual bytes and on demand for block space, not on the amount sent. Rates are quoted in satoshis per virtual byte (sat/vB) and move with network traffic, so the wallet’s current estimate is the figure to check. Lightning works differently, because each node that forwards a payment can charge a base fee plus a small share of the amount.

The deposit is ready to send once four things check out.

  • The route and network are ones the cashier lists.
  • The pasted address or invoice matches the cashier in full.
  • The amount that arrives meets the platform’s minimum.
  • The fee shown in the wallet has been checked.

The user then approves the payment in the wallet or exchange and keeps the transaction ID (TXID) or Lightning payment record until the balance updates.

How Long Does a Bitcoin Transaction Take?

An on-chain Bitcoin deposit usually reaches a platform balance within 10 to 60 minutes, and a Lightning payment within seconds. The wait covers the wallet or exchange sending the payment, the confirmations the platform requires and the crediting of the balance.

Blocks arrive about every ten minutes on average, so three required confirmations mean roughly half an hour. Miners prioritize transactions with higher fee rates, so a low fee can mean a much longer wait. Lightning can be delayed or fail when no path to the receiver is found.

What to Do When a Bitcoin Deposit Goes Wrong

The next step depends on whether the payment was sent, confirmed or credited.

Crypto Sent to the Wrong Network or Address

Sending crypto over a network the cashier doesn’t list, such as wrapped BTC (BEP-20 or ERC-20) instead of native Bitcoin, can mean the deposit is lost entirely. A block explorer shows where the coins went. If they reached the platform, support can look into it with the TXID, while coins sent to someone else’s address only come back if that person returns them.

Bitcoin Transaction Unconfirmed or Pending

A transaction that pays too little waits in the mempool, the queue of unconfirmed transactions, while miners pick ones with higher fee rates. Some wallets support replace-by-fee (RBF), which swaps it for a version that pays more.

Expired Lightning Invoice

The user creates a new invoice in the cashier and pays that, since an expired one shouldn’t be paid.

Deposit Confirmed but Not Credited

The user sends support the TXID, amount, network and receiving address when a block explorer shows the confirmations the platform requires but the balance hasn’t moved.

How to Spend Bitcoin Responsibly on Entertainment Platforms

Deposit limits and self-exclusion, where the platform offers them, keep spending in check. Where the user lives decides the minimum legal age and whether these platforms are legal at all. New crypto entertainment platforms often hold offshore licenses from Anjouan or Curaçao, so the license, accepted countries and identity check terms deserve a read before the first deposit.

In the US, the national support helpline offers confidential support around the clock by call or text at 1-800-MY-RESET and through online chat. A platform balance is no place to store crypto, and only money the user can afford to lose belongs in one.

title: Singapore Issues S$100M Tokenized MAS Bills, Testing Wholesale CBDC Settlement at Scale
summary:
Key Takeaways: MAS had issued S$100 million in tokenized bills settled using wholesale CBDC. Five major dealers were competing in the auction, and they bid in excess of double the
The post Singapore Issues S$100M Tokenized MAS Bills, Testing Wholesale CBDC Settlement at Scale appeared first on Crypt...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • MAS had issued S$100 million in tokenized bills settled using wholesale CBDC.
  • Five major dealers were competing in the auction, and they bid in excess of double the bid price.
  • Singapore is looking to scale down the bills and collateral tokenization in 2027 through live trials.

Singapore completes live issuance of S$100 million in tokenized MAS Bills using its own wholesale CBDC-based distributed ledger infrastructure.

The transaction adds tokenised securities to a network with central bank money, providing Singapore with another real-world test of using the blockchain for financial settlement.

  • Tokenized MAS Bills Settle Directly With Wholesale CBDC
    • Native Issuance Changes the Settlement Flow
  • Tokenized Bills Could Become Onchain Collateral
    • Singapore Dollar Test Network Becomes SG Digital Ledger

Tokenized MAS Bills Settle Directly With Wholesale CBDC

MAS issued the four-week bills on Nov. 6 through the Singapore Dollar Test Network. The securities were really issued and tokenized in one fell swoop, not through the traditional chain, but natively as a token.

That design minimizes the need for reconciliations between the traditional records and the blockchain representation, MAS said.

Applications for the sale were worth a total of more than twice of the S$100 million being issued. DBS, HSBC Singapore, OCBC, Standard Chartered Singapore and UOB were among the five major dealers. The bills will be due and payable Dec. 4.

Read More: Singapore and Germany Test Wholesale CBDC FX Settlement With Zero-Knowledge Proofs

Native Issuance Changes the Settlement Flow

The main advantage is that the MAS Bills are placed on top of the distributed ledger. The transaction was settled on the same test system, with the asset leg and cash leg settled digitally via wholesale CBDC.

This structure has importance in tokenized markets as securities may be moved against central bank money without the need for having to operate multiple settlement systems. Wholesale CBDC, regulated stablecoins and tokenized bank deposits are expected to contribute to the tokenized markets, says MAS Managing Director Chia Der Jiun.

Tokenized Bills Could Become Onchain Collateral

The issuance follows Singapore’s interbank overnight lending settled on a wholesale CBDC that took place during a live trial last year.

The network now has a tokenized SGD denominated asset, which can be utilized in secured lending or collateralization arrangements, by accepting tokenized MAS Bills.

MAS will expand issuance scale and add more financial institutions to its network, and trials of various applications of collateral management will follow in 2027.

This is not only for placing bonds on a blockchain but for every other use case beyond that. Eventually, tokenized collateral would be expected to enable quicker movement of assets between counterparties and supply operational simplicity for lending and settlement.

Singapore Dollar Test Network Becomes SG Digital Ledger

MAS is also in the process of changing the name of Singapore Dollar Test Network to SG Digital Ledger. The infrastructure is geared towards adoption of tokenised financial assets, with transactions extended beyond isolated proof-of-concept projects.

As asset tokenization and adoption of digital money expands, trusted CBDC-based settlement will have greater significance, especially in large-value transactions where settlement certainty is paramount, Chia said at the Singapore FinTech Festival.

The Singaporean Government is also creating frameworks for tokenization, such as Project Guardian for tokenized funds and bonds, as well as tokenized stablecoins for institutional markets.

To mark the ANTx listing, Bitrue is running a Trade & Earn campaign in which traders share a 20,000 USDT prize pool, with up to 1,250 USDT per person.

Anthropic Arrives on Public Markets

Anthropic, the AI company behind the Claude family of models, is listed on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker ANT, with trading beginning on Nov. 19, 2026. The offering is one of the most closely watched listings of the year and has drawn strong interest from crypto platforms, several of which are offering tokenized access to the stock around the debut.

For crypto traders, tokenized stocks offer a way to follow companies like Anthropic without leaving the crypto ecosystem, using stablecoins and the same accounts they already use for digital assets.

What Is ANTx

ANTx is a tokenized stock from xStocks that tracks the price of Anthropic shares. According to information published for the launch, each ANTx token is backed 1:1 by Anthropic shares held in custody by Backed Assets (JE) Limited. ANTx holders gain price exposure to Anthropic, but do not receive shareholder or voting rights.

On Bitrue, ANTx trades on the spot market against USDT.

Bitrue’s Anthropic Product Lineup

With the ANTx listing, Bitrue now offers three ways to trade Anthropic-related products:

  • ANTx spot trading (xStocks): spot trading of the tokenized Anthropic stock against USDT, available from day one.
  • ANT/USDT perpetual futures: a USDT-settled perpetual futures contract tracking Anthropic, live on Bitrue Futures since Nov. 17. This product is separate from xStocks and is supported by Bitrue’s RWA trading event.
  • ANT3L and ANT3S leveraged tokens: leveraged long and short tokens linked to Anthropic, expected to list on Nov. 20. These are also separate from xStocks.

Together, the three products let traders choose how they follow Anthropic, from spot exposure through a tokenized stock to futures and leveraged tokens.

Trade & Earn: 20,000 USDT Prize Pool

To mark the ANTx listing, Bitrue is running a Trade & Earn campaign for ANTx spot trading:

  • Prize pool: 20,000 USDT shared among eligible traders.

Full campaign rules, including the campaign period and eligibility, are available on the campaign page.

“Anthropic’s public debut is one of the biggest moments of the year at the intersection of AI and markets, and our users want to be part of it,” Bitrue said in a statement. “By supporting ANTx from day one, alongside ANT futures and leveraged tokens, we are giving our users several ways to follow Anthropic from the same account they use for crypto.”

Part of Bitrue’s Growing RWA Range

title: Anthropic Stock (ANT) Debuts on Nasdaq at $1.5 Trillion Valuation in Record-Breaking IPO
summary: Anthropic is entering the public market with a record $81.3 billion IPO, pricing shares at $83 and setting a fully diluted valuation of approximately $1.5 trillion.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: ANT

Anthropic is entering the public market with a record $81.3 billion IPO, pricing shares at $83 and setting a fully diluted valuation of approximately $1.5 trillion.

The Claude developer’s Nasdaq listing under the ticker ANT marks a significant moment for the artificial intelligence industry, as investors assess whether its rapid revenue growth can support its extraordinary market valuation.

Anthropic Raises $81.3 Billion in Record IPO

Anthropic priced its initial public offering at $83 per share on November 18, above its previously marketed range of $70 to $78. The offering includes 980 million Class A shares, making it the largest IPO by proceeds raised to date.

Founded in 2021 by former OpenAI executives led by Dario Amodei, Anthropic reported $33 billion in nine-month revenue, marking year-over-year growth of more than 1,200%. Source: @WhaleInsider/X

Strong investor demand allowed the company to expand its original offering from 825 million shares, an increase of approximately 19%. Anthropic is selling 956,351,354 shares, while existing shareholders are offering another 23,648,646 shares. The company will not receive proceeds from the shares sold by those existing investors.

At the final offering price, the IPO generated approximately $81.3 billion in gross proceeds. The valuation reaches roughly $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis, accounting for securities such as stock options and restricted stock units. On a non-diluted basis, the company’s valuation stands at approximately $1.1 trillion.

The transaction also includes a separate $26 billion private placement at the IPO price, bringing the combined deal value to approximately $107.3 billion. This additional financing increases the capital available to support Anthropic’s expansion beyond the public offering itself.

Anthropic shares are scheduled to begin trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on November 19 under the ticker ANT. The listing process is expected to make the stock eligible for trading at approximately 10:00 a.m. ET, following the exchange’s opening procedures.

Claude Developer’s Revenue Surges More Than 1,200%

Founded in 2021 by former OpenAI executives and researchers, Anthropic has developed into one of the most closely watched companies in the generative AI industry. Chief Executive Officer Dario Amodei co-founded the business with a group of former OpenAI colleagues, positioning the company around advanced AI development and safety.

Anthropic’s $81.3 billion IPO surpassed SpaceX’s $75 billion offering in June 2026, setting a new record for the largest IPO in history. Source: @EconomyApp/X

Its Claude family of models has become the foundation of its commercial operations. The company’s offerings include consumer AI products, enterprise services, and developer-focused tools such as Claude Code, which has gained traction among software developers.

Anthropic’s latest financial disclosures highlight the speed of its expansion. Revenue reached $33.2 billion during the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared with $2.5 billion in the corresponding period a year earlier. The increase represents year-over-year growth of approximately 1,206%.

Customer adoption has also expanded considerably. Anthropic reported more than 11,900 customers generating at least $100,000 in annualized revenue over the preceding 12 months as of September 30. That figure compares with more than 950 customers a year earlier, illustrating the company’s growing presence among enterprise buyers.

The company also reported an annualized revenue run rate of approximately $81 billion as of October 31, according to its IPO disclosures cited by Reuters. This figure reflects the pace of business at that point rather than revenue already earned over a full year.

However, Anthropic has cautioned against assuming that its recent growth rate will continue. Its prospectus states, “We do not expect our revenue will continue to grow at comparable rates,” highlighting the uncertainty surrounding the long-term economics of the rapidly evolving AI market.

AI Infrastructure Spending Raises Profitability Questions

Despite its revenue expansion, Anthropic continues to face substantial expenses associated with developing, training, and operating advanced AI models.

The company’s SEC filing reported an operating loss of $1.3 billion for the first nine months of 2026, down from $5.2 billion in the same period of 2025. Although the reduction indicates an improvement in operating performance, the company has yet to establish consistent operating profitability.

Anthropic has committed approximately $900.9 billion to computing and infrastructure, with $70.7 billion due within 12 months of September 30, according to its final prospectus. Source: @IPONewsroom_/X

Computing requirements remain a central financial challenge. Anthropic spent nearly $9 billion on computing capacity and infrastructure during the first half of 2026, according to Reuters. It incurred another $5 billion in computing costs during the third quarter.

The company has also committed to nearly $900 billion in future computing capacity through infrastructure partners, including Amazon and Alphabet’s Google. These arrangements are intended to provide the resources required to train and operate increasingly capable models.

Such commitments expose Anthropic to financing, infrastructure delivery, and demand-related risks. The company has warned in its regulatory filing that difficulties affecting its infrastructure partners could delay, reduce, or increase the cost of contracted computing capacity.

Competition presents another challenge. Anthropic faces pressure from OpenAI, Google, and developers of open-weight AI models, while some enterprise customers are also exploring the development of internal AI systems to manage costs.

The company’s ability to retain customers, improve computing efficiency, and maintain its position in enterprise AI will therefore remain important considerations for public-market investors.

Anthropic IPO Becomes a Test for AI Stock Demand

Anthropic’s Nasdaq debut arrives as investors reconsider the valuations and spending requirements of the broader AI industry. The company’s record fundraising demonstrates substantial demand for exposure to advanced AI development, even as concerns about infrastructure costs and future profitability remain.

The listing also provides an important reference point for other privately held AI businesses considering public offerings. Anthropic’s closest competitor, OpenAI, has also been discussed as a potential candidate for a future stock-market listing.

Investors will now have access to publicly traded Anthropic shares and regular financial disclosures, bringing greater scrutiny to the company’s revenue growth, operating expenses, capital commitments, and competitive position.

As portfolio manager Armina Rosenberg told Reuters, “One listing won’t settle the debate.” Her assessment reflects the broader uncertainty surrounding whether the economics of advanced AI can support the substantial valuations currently assigned to the industry’s fastest-growing companies.

For Anthropic, the $83 IPO price and approximately $1.5 trillion fully diluted valuation establish the starting point for its public-market journey. Its performance as a listed company will increasingly depend on converting rapid customer adoption into sustainable financial results.

title: Hashi Mainnet is Live With 20-Plus Partners, Bringing Bitcoin Finance to Sui at Scale
summary: Grand Cayman, Cayman Islands, 19th November 2026, Chainwire
content:
Skip to content

Grand Cayman, Cayman Islands, 19th November 2026, Chainwire

Grand Cayman, Cayman Islands, November 19th, 2026, Chainwire

Anchorage Digital, Fluid, HoneyB, and Upshift support institutional and retail access to Bitcoin on Sui with BitGo, Inc. expected to follow in 2027

Hashi, Sui’s native Bitcoin finance infrastructure, is now live on mainnet, with more than 20 custody, retail, and DeFi participants.

Bitcoin has spent years becoming one of the world’s largest pools of capital. Now the infrastructure to put it to work has arrived, forming one of the broadest coalitions in Bitcoin finance. 

That coalition is still growing fast. The latest to join Hashi are Merkl, an onchain incentive platform; and Current, a lending protocol. These additions expand the ecosystem of DeFi products and services being built around Bitcoin on Sui.

Bitcoin-Native Finance, Now Live

Hashi keeps Bitcoin on the Bitcoin network and mints hBTC, a 1:1 Bitcoin-backed asset, on Sui. That hBTC can then serve as collateral for lending, borrowing, and other onchain financial products. 

Hashi is decentralized by design. It’s secured by validators, not a single entity, using industry-leading cryptography. On top of that foundation, it connects leading providers across custody, trading, and decentralized finance to build financial products, giving Bitcoin holders many ways to put their assets to work.

Accessing Bitcoin Finance on Sui

With hBTC now live, Bitcoin holders have a new set of opportunities at their fingertips. That starts with borrowing against BTC and accessing new financial strategies through lending markets and vaults. 

To meet the specific needs of institutions, several new providers are offering new lending and vault facilities. 

Fluid’s institutional-grade lending protocol is now live on Sui, beginning with Bitcoin-backed stablecoin loans. Bitcoin holders can use Hashi to bring BTC onto Sui as hBTC, then use it as collateral on Fluid to borrow stablecoins, starting with USDC with more flows coming. 

“Bitcoin is the largest pool of idle capital in crypto,” said Samyak Jain, founder and CEO at Fluid. “With Hashi, it can now power deep, capital-efficient credit markets on Fluid.”

Institutional Access, Retail Opportunities, and Liquidity

For institutions, that infrastructure shows up as a custody problem solved. Institutions will be able to use both leading crypto custodians, Anchorage Digital and BitGo, Inc. (“BitGo”) to access Hashi. This model gives institutions a path to hold or deploy BTC into Hashi. Previously announced institutional partners, such as Cumberland and Wave Digital Assets will all play roles as early participants in deploying BTC and stablecoins on Hashi, providing liquidity to a variety of strategies on Sui. Sui DeFi protocols, including Blueprint Finance (Concrete), Bluefin, Cetus, Current, and Suilend will also unlock new lending opportunities, stablecoin credit, and yield strategies backed by Bitcoin. 

“Some of the world’s largest Bitcoin holders are sitting on enormous amounts of untapped financial potential,” said Nathan McCauley, CEO and Co-Founder at Anchorage Digital. “Hashi gives our institutional clients a new way to access Bitcoin finance on Sui, with their BTC held in custody at Anchorage Digital Bank.”

If you’re an institution interested in deploying BTC or stablecoins on Hashi, please reach out to your custodian or [email protected]. Users can explore more at sui.io/hashi. 

About Sui

Sui, where money moves as freely as messages, is a next-generation Layer 1 blockchain built for agentic finance and scalable global payments. Founded by the core team behind Meta’s stablecoin initiative and powered by an object-centric model, Sui makes assets, permissions, and user data programmable and ownable. Sui’s primitives offer builders everything they need to create high-performance payments and financial applications, including instant agentic payments. Learn more at sui.io.

title: OmenX announces $2 million in funding from Informed Ventures and launches on-demand 30-second Bitcoin predictions
summary: The Base-native leveraged prediction market platform expands its offering across crypto, global financial assets, sports and esports. Toronto, November 19, 2026 – OmenX, a Base-native leveraged prediction market platform, today announced $2 million in funding from Informed Ventures alongside the lau...
content:
The Base-native leveraged prediction market platform expands its offering across crypto, global financial assets, sports and esports.

Toronto, November 19, 2026 – OmenX, a Base-native leveraged prediction market platform, today announced $2 million in funding from Informed Ventures alongside the launch of its on-demand, 30-second Bitcoin price prediction product.

The new product lets users predict whether Bitcoin’s price will rise or fall over the next 30 seconds, with each trade starting its own prediction window. A position opened at 10:00:12 runs until 10:00:42. Users can act when their view forms, with a full 30-second horizon, rather than adapting to the remaining time in a shared market round.

Featuring zero-slippage execution and rapid settlement, the product extends the familiar five- and fifteen-minute crypto prediction format to a shorter, individually timed experience. It adds to OmenX’s intraday offering, which spans prediction horizons from 30 seconds to 24 hours, depending on the market.

Beyond crypto, OmenX offers directional prediction markets linked to more than 100 global assets, including U.S. equities, futures, ETFs and indices. Its event markets also cover live sports and esports, with sports coverage spanning major football leagues, basketball, American football, ice hockey, baseball and UFC.

Leverage has been central to OmenX’s platform from the outset, allowing traders to amplify their exposure on supported event markets. The latest launch builds on that foundation while advancing a broader goal: making prediction markets a practical financial tool for retail users.

OmenX organizes the trading decision around a defined question: will an asset’s price be higher or lower at the end of a specified period? Users can express a directional view without purchasing the underlying asset, targeting an exact closing price or constructing an options position that requires decisions about strikes, implied volatility and time decay.

“Leverage has been part of OmenX from the start, but our ambition goes beyond adding leverage to prediction markets,” said James, founder and CEO of OmenX. “We want to make global markets easier to participate in. A trader should be able to take a view on Bitcoin, a stock or a sporting event and express it through a clear contract and a timeframe that fits their judgment.”

The platform’s emphasis on short, recurring markets provides faster feedback on trading decisions and can reduce the time capital remains committed to individual outcomes. OmenX plans to expand its coverage of traditional and crypto assets while deepening the trading experience across supported markets.

About OmenX

OmenX is a Base-native leveraged prediction market platform covering crypto, global financial assets, live sports and esports. Through defined outcomes, short settlement cycles and leverage on supported markets, OmenX is building a more accessible way to trade market views.

Learn more at omenx.com.

title: My Wallet Introduces 1:1 Cross-Chain Stablecoin Swaps After Being Listed First on WalletConnect
summary: Dubai, United Arab Emirates, 19th November 2026, Chainwire
content:
Skip to content

Dubai, United Arab Emirates, 19th November 2026, Chainwire

Dubai, United Arab Emirates, November 19th, 2026, Chainwire

My Wallet users can now receive a different stablecoin on another blockchain at a fixed 1:1 token rate on eligible routes, with no spread, slippage or swap fee charged by the wallet

My Wallet, a self-custodial, open-source crypto wallet serving more than 10 million users, has launched 1:1 swaps for USDT, USDC, USDe and USDS across supported blockchains. On eligible routes, users can switch both stablecoins and networks within a single in-app flow, with the amount they will receive fixed before confirmation. 

The launch follows My Wallet’s listing at the top of WalletConnect’s WalletGuide. The wallet is also WalletConnect Certified and connects users to more than 80,000 compatible apps.

Simplifying Stablecoin Transfers Across Blockchains

According to research published in October 2026 by Coinbase and The Block Pro Research, organic stablecoin transfer volume exceeded $400 million per hour during Q3 2026. Yet stablecoins operate across multiple blockchains and token issuers, creating friction when users need a specific token on a specific network. Even when funds arrive on the right network, users may still hold the wrong stablecoin for a payment, trade or application.

My Wallet addresses this through its in-app swap aggregator, powered by LayerZero, NEAR Intents, and other bridges resulting in the best rate. On eligible stablecoin routes, the aggregator offers a fixed 1:1 token rate, with no exchange-rate spread, slippage or My Wallet swap commission. My Wallet is the first among major crypto wallets to offer 1:1 swaps between different stablecoins across blockchains in a single in-app flow.

How the 1:1 Stablecoin Swaps Work

The fixed 1:1 rate can apply whether users switch to a different stablecoin or move the same token to another blockchain. On a supported cross-chain USDT-to-USDC route, for example, a user sending 10,000 USDT receives exactly 10,000 USDC. The same rate applies when the token stays the same: a supported transfer of 10,000 USDT from Ethereum to TRON delivers exactly 10,000 USDT on TRON.

The 1:1 option is available for swaps above $30 on supported routes. There is no exchange-rate spread, slippage or My Wallet swap commission. Applicable blockchain network fees are paid separately, and the exact destination token amount is shown before confirmation. Other routes may have different rates and fees.

“Stablecoins are supposed to make moving money simpler, but users still have to think about which token they hold and which blockchain it’s on,” said Alexander Zinchuk, founder of My Wallet. “We’re removing that friction. If you hold USDT and need USDC on another network, you should be able to make that change in one step, know exactly how many tokens you’ll receive, and not pay an additional swap commission to your wallet.”

Native Bitcoin and Gasless EVM Transfers

The stablecoin launch follows the introduction of native Bitcoin support in My Wallet. Users can hold, send, receive and swap BTC alongside assets on Ethereum, Solana, TON and other networks, as well as buy Bitcoin with a bank card or sell it for fiat through MoonPay.

My Wallet now supports gasless transfers on Ethereum, Base, BNB Chain, Arbitrum and Optimism, adding to the existing support on Solana and TON. For these EVM transfers, the network fee is deducted from the tokens being sent, so users do not need to acquire a separate native token for gas. Supported assets are USDC on all five EVM networks, USDT on Ethereum and BNB Chain, bridged USDT on Base and Optimism, and USDT0 on Arbitrum. There is no minimum transfer amount or daily limit on the number of transactions.

Together, these innovative features advance My Wallet’s broader “All You Need to Enjoy Crypto” vision, combining asset management, seamless trading, and ease of use into one self-custodial app.

The new features are already available in My Wallet. Swap availability is subject to the selected assets, networks and routes.

About My Wallet

My Wallet is a self-custodial, open-source multichain wallet for Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, Hyperliquid, TON, TRON, BNB, Base, Robinhood, Monad, Arbitrum, Polygon, and more. Founded in 2022, My Wallet serves over 10 million users across mobile, desktop, web and its Telegram Mini App. The wallet has been audited by CertiK and ranks among the top-5 wallets on CertiK’s Wallet Leaderboard.

My Wallet is WalletConnect Certified and currently listed 1st in WalletConnect’s WalletGuide, connecting users to more than 80,000 compatible apps.

Staking inside My Wallet is powered by Stakee, its own staking protocol, ranked among the top-2 TON DeFi protocols by TVL on DefiLlama.

For more details, users can visit mywallet.io and try My Wallet at mywallet.io/get.

title: WSDT introduces prop trading for crypto and tokenized US stocks
summary: One-step challenges start at $19, with a free demo and weekly competitions available in the same trading terminal DUBAI, UAE, November 18, 2026 – WSDT is introducing its prop trading platform for cryptocurrency perpetual futures, gold and tokenized US stocks. Traders can access these markets through...
content:
One-step challenges start at $19, with a free demo and weekly competitions available in the same trading terminal

DUBAI, UAE, November 18, 2026 – WSDT is introducing its prop trading platform for cryptocurrency perpetual futures, gold and tokenized US stocks. Traders can access these markets through a single simulated account, with one-step evaluations starting at a one-time fee of $19 for a $1,500 account.

The platform combines crypto perpetual futures, including Bitcoin and Ethereum, with xStocks instruments tracking companies such as Apple, NVIDIA and Tesla, alongside stock-index ETFs. Perpetual futures are contracts without an expiry date; xStocks track the prices of underlying shares or ETFs. On WSDT, these instruments are traded in a simulated environment, without ownership of the underlying shares or tokens.

Positions across the markets share the same account balance and count toward the same evaluation. Traders can work across crypto and equity-linked instruments in one terminal while managing a single set of account limits.

One evaluation, published trading rules

A WSDT challenge tests trading performance against a 10% profit target, a 4% daily loss limit and a 6% maximum drawdown fixed against the starting account size. Traders must trade on at least four separate days, with no deadline to complete the evaluation. Account sizes range from $1,500 to $200,000, with fees varying by size.

Traders who pass move to a funded-stage account, which is also simulated and retains the loss limits. They receive 80% of eligible profits under WSDT’s Provider Service Agreement. The evaluation fee pays for access to the challenge; it is not a trading deposit.

Free ways to try the platform

Registered users can open a free 14-day demo with a $100,000 simulated balance, without providing a payment card or making a deposit. The demo uses the same terminal as challenges, allowing traders to practice before entering an evaluation. Demo results do not qualify for payouts.

WSDT also runs an ongoing weekly competition with free entry. Every participant starts with a $240,000 simulated balance, and the top three finishers receive challenge accounts. A new round opens each Monday at noon New York time. Winners must pass their awarded challenge before progressing to the funded stage.

Registration, account options and full challenge rules are available on the WSDT website.

About WSDT

WSDT provides trader evaluation and educational services across crypto, gold and tokenized equity instruments. Built by TEFS, a prop trading firm established in 2017, it is operated by TEFS Marketing Management L.L.C. in Dubai, UAE. All WSDT trading accounts are simulated.

Geneva, Switzerland –  TRON DAO, the community-governed DAO dedicated to accelerating the decentralization of the internet through blockchain technology and decentralized applications (dApps), today announced that the Aave App, a high-yield savings mobile app developed and managed by Aave Labs, will add support for USDT (TRC-20) deposits on the TRON network as it expands to Android following its initial launch on iOS.

The launch combines Android’s global reach with TRON’s leading role in the stablecoin ecosystem, expanding mobile access to onchain savings opportunities that are not accessible on traditional savings apps. With support for USDT on TRON, eligible users in supported jurisdictions can now deposit USDT on TRON and start earning yield on their savings.

Android’s extensive global footprint offers a significant distribution opportunity for digital asset applications, particularly in markets where stablecoins are used for payments, remittances, and savings. TRON provides an established infrastructure for this opportunity, with more than $94 billion in circulating USDT, the largest circulating supply of Tether’s dollar-pegged stablecoin among blockchain networks. TRON also supports a broad range of stablecoin use cases, including payments, cross-border transfers, and digital asset transactions.

Aave is building the World’s Savings App, a simple, globally accessible tool designed to help people grow and manage their savings, with a delightful design experience on the surface and powerful onchain finance infrastructure working under the hood. Users of the app can earn yield on their savings, enjoy flexible access to their funds, and benefit from the Balance Protection program. They can also deposit and withdraw via stablecoins or banks in eligible countries and project their potential savings growth over the years with a future simulator. Following its availability on iOS, the Android launch expands the app’s mobile reach, while TRON support connects users to one of the largest USDT ecosystems in onchain finance.

“Aave Labs has a proven track record of building leading DeFi products, and the Aave App brings that expertise to everyday users,” said Justin Sun, Founder of TRON. “With TRON support on Android and iOS, more people can use the USDT they already hold on TRON to access simple, accessible onchain savings with the Aave App.”

“Millions of people in emerging economies already rely on stablecoins on TRON to save and send money,” said Stani Kulechov, Founder and CEO of Aave Labs. “The Aave App lets them earn on those dollars.”

By enabling USDT deposits through the Aave App on Android, the integration connects TRON’s established stablecoin ecosystem with a consumer-focused mobile application. The launch reflects the continued convergence of mobile applications and blockchain infrastructure, as consumer-focused products work to make digital assets and decentralized financial services more accessible worldwide.

About TRON DAO

TRON DAO is a community-governed DAO dedicated to accelerating the decentralization of the internet via blockchain technology and dApps.

Founded in September 2017, the TRON blockchain has experienced significant growth since its MainNet launch in May 2018. Today, TRON hosts the largest circulating supply of USD Tether (USDT) stablecoin, which currently exceeds $94 billion. As of November 2026, the TRON blockchain has recorded over 414 million in total user accounts, more than 16 billion in total transactions, and over $24 billion in total value locked (TVL), based on TRONSCAN. Recognized as the global settlement layer for stablecoin transactions and everyday purchases with proven success, TRON is “Moving Trillions, Empowering Billions.”

About Aave Labs

Aave Labs is a core contributor in the Aave network and builds products that make saving, lending and borrowing simple and accessible worldwide. Aave is the world’s largest onchain lending network, with more than $30 billion in net deposits. Users, fintechs and financial institutions use it to earn interest on stablecoins and other assets and to borrow against them, 24/7, with every transaction visible onchain. The network is governed by the Aave DAO, where AAVE holders vote on changes to the network and its treasury.

Aave Labs’ products include Aave App, a savings app for everyone; Aave Pro, for advanced lending and borrowing; Aave Kit, which lets fintechs and businesses offer savings and loans to their users; and Aave Horizon, an institutional platform for borrowing stablecoins against tokenized real-world assets. For more information, visit aave.com.
